le lezard rouge (train historique de met.d: A metric-gauge tourist train traveling through the Selja Gorges between Metlaoui and Redeyef, on the former phosphate mining line. Rolling stock from a former Bey’s train. Station coordinates (approximate).
le lezard rouge (train historique de met.a: A metric-gauge tourist train, featuring the Bey's vintage rolling stock, winds its way through the Selja Gorge.
le lezard rouge (train historique de met.c: Book in advance during peak season and bring plenty of water; the tour departs from Metlaoui.

ksar ouled debbab.d: A fortified ksar with ghorfas near Tataouine, partly built into the rock, situated on a hill. Designated a national monument in January 2024.
ksar ouled debbab.a: A fortified ksar with ghorfas, partly built into the rock, situated on a hill near Tataouine; designated a national monument.
ksar ouled debbab.c: Unobstructed view from the ksar: the late-afternoon light is the most beautiful.

ksar jouamaa.d: Stone ksar in Beni Khedache (Medenine), built around 1770. A fortified communal granary designated a Tunisian historic monument.
ksar jouamaa.a: A fortified communal granary built of Beni Khedache stone, constructed around 1770.
ksar jouamaa.c: Mountain location: Be sure to bring water and shoes suitable for the terrain.

ksar beni barka.d: A fortified ksar with ghorfas in the Tataouine Governorate, formerly a communal granary for the region's tribes.
ksar beni barka.a: Ksar a Ghorfas, a former communal granary used by the tribes of the Tataouine region.
ksar beni barka.c: A short visit; can be combined with the other nearby ksour in Dahar.

metameur (ksar).d: A village located about 7 km northwest of Medenine, founded around the 14th century, known for its ksar with vaulted ghorfas on several levels. It is one of the best-preserved in the south.
metameur (ksar).a: A village whose ksar, with its vaulted ghorfas on several levels, is one of the best-preserved in the south.
metameur (ksar).c: 7 km from Medenine—an easy stop; the light is perfect for photos at the end of the day.

ghomrassen.d: A town in the southeast, about 26 km from Tataouine, a former Berber settlement in a valley of cliffs and cave granaries.
ghomrassen.a: An ancient Berber settlement in a valley of cliffs dotted with cave granaries.
ghomrassen.c: A convenient starting point for exploring the surrounding ksour; bring water.

ksar ouled m'hemed.d: Fortified granary in Ghorfas (Tataouine), built around 1855, with approximately 223 storage cells on three levels. Restored in 2007 in collaboration with the INP.
ksar ouled m'hemed.a: Fortified granary with ghorfas (circa 1855), comprising approximately 223 storage cells on three levels, restored in collaboration with the INP.
ksar ouled m'hemed.c: A quick visit; can be combined with the neighboring ksours of Tataouine.

ksar ouled brahim (medenine).d: A ksar in downtown Medenine, square in shape with sides measuring approximately 80 m, featuring ~140 vaulted ghorfas on two levels. A testament to the city’s ksar district.
ksar ouled brahim (medenine).a: A square ksar measuring approximately 80 m on each side, with about 140 vaulted ghorfas on two levels, a testament to the ksar district of Medenine.
ksar ouled brahim (medenine).c: In town: within walking distance when visiting Medenine.

ksar megabla.d: An oval-shaped ksar on the outskirts of Tataouine, founded around 1400, with numerous ghorfas on two to four levels.
ksar megabla.a: An oval-shaped ksar on the outskirts of Tataouine, featuring numerous ghorfas on two to four levels.
ksar megabla.c: A short leg just outside Tataouine; expect hot weather.

ksar tamelest.d: Ksar a Ghorfas in the Tataouine Governorate, the former fortified granary of the Dahar.
ksar tamelest.a: A former fortified granary with ghorfas in Dahar, in the Tataouine Governorate.
ksar tamelest.c: A modest site; best visited as part of a guided tour of the ksour of Dahar.

ksar ezzahra.d: A mountain ksar at the foot of Djebel Abiodh, southeast of Tataouine, consisting of a square-shaped old section and the more recent Ksar Jedid. Designated a historic monument in January 2024.
ksar ezzahra.a: A mountain ksar at the foot of Djebel Abiodh, featuring a square-shaped old section and a more recent Ksar Jedid; designated a historic monument.
ksar ezzahra.c: Mountain Access Southeast of Tataouine: Drive Carefully and Bring Water.

borj el kebir (borj ghazi mustapha, djer.d: The coastal fort at Houmt Souk, the largest and best-preserved on Djerba, was rebuilt in the 16th century. It is associated with the corsair Dragut.
borj el kebir (borj ghazi mustapha, djer.a: The largest coastal fort on Djerba, located in Houmt Souk, was rebuilt in the 16th century and is associated with the corsair Dragut.
borj el kebir (borj ghazi mustapha, djer.c: Climb up to the ramparts for a view of the harbor; there's very little shade, so be sure to bring a hat.

houmt souk (djerba).d: The main city and capital of Djerba, built on the site of an ancient city. It features a medina, traditional souks, and historic fondouks.
houmt souk (djerba).a: The capital of Djerba: the medina, traditional souks, and historic fondouks.
houmt souk (djerba).c: Stroll through the souks in the morning or in the evening, when the heat has subsided.
houmt souk (djerba).leg: Djerba is traditionally identified as the Island of the Lotophagi, the “lotus-eaters”: in *The Odyssey*, Odysseus’s companions taste a fruit there so sweet that they forget to return home. Homer saw it as a land of blissful oblivion.

guellala (djerba).d: A village in southern Djerba, known as a historic center of pottery thanks to its clay deposits. The tradition of ceramics dates back to antiquity, with workshops and cave kilns.
guellala (djerba).a: A village in southern Djerba, a historic center for pottery, featuring workshops and cave kilns.
guellala (djerba).c: Visit a potter's workshop; the shops are clustered along the main road.

mosquee d'el may (djerba).d: A fortified Ibadite mosque in the center of Djerba, with whitewashed walls and a stocky minaret. Designated a historic monument in 1928, it serves the defensive role typical of the island’s mosques.
mosquee d'el may (djerba).a: A fortified Ibadite mosque with whitewashed walls and a stocky minaret, listed as a historic site since 1928.
mosquee d'el may (djerba).c: Be sure to admire the fortified exterior; the interior can be reserved for the faithful.

mosquee fadhloun (djerba).d: A 14th-century Ibadite mosque on the outskirts of Midoun, featuring the simple, fortified architecture typical of Djerba. Listed in 2022.
mosquee fadhloun (djerba).a: A 14th-century Ibadite mosque with simple, fortified architecture, located on the outskirts of Midoun.
mosquee fadhloun (djerba).c: A beautiful, solitary white silhouette: perfect for photographing in soft light.

erriadh (hara seghira, djerba).d: A village south of Houmt Souk, a historic neighborhood with a large Jewish community (Hara Sghira). Home to the Ghriba Synagogue and the Djerbahood murals (2014).
erriadh (hara seghira, djerba).a: A historic neighborhood with a large Jewish community, home to the Ghriba Synagogue and the Djerbahood street murals (2014).
erriadh (hara seghira, djerba).c: Stroll through the narrow streets on foot to discover the murals; go early in the morning to catch the light.

tamezret.d: A Berber village nestled on the slopes of one of the highest peaks in the Matmata Mountains (~480 m), about 40 km southwest of Gabès. An Amazigh-speaking community (Chelha).
tamezret.a: A Berber village nestled on the slopes of one of the highest peaks in the Matmata Mountains, home to an Amazigh-speaking community (Chelha).
tamezret.c: Mountain views: Head up to the upper village for the view; bring water.

zraoua.d: A Berber village perched on a plateau in the Matmata Mountains (Nouvelle Matmata, Gabès). The inhabitants migrated to a village on the plain in the late 1970s.
zraoua.a: A Berber village perched on a plateau in the Matmata Mountains, which has been partially deserted since the late 1970s.
zraoua.c: Arid mountain terrain: Be sure to bring water and sturdy shoes.

taoujout.d: A Berber village in the Matmata Mountains (Gabès), near Tamezret and Zraoua, where the Chelha Amazigh language is traditionally spoken.
taoujout.a: A Berber village in the Matmata Mountains, near Tamezret and Zraoua, with an Amazigh-speaking (Chelha) tradition.
taoujout.c: Best combined with Tamezret; this is a mountain road, so drive carefully.

beni khedache.d: The city and district of Medenine (~30 km west), located between Jebel Dahar and the Grand Erg Oriental. Ksour, a fortified granary, and an underground mosque.
beni khedache.a: A village between Jebel Dahar and the Grand Erg, surrounded by ksour, a fortified granary, and an underground mosque.
beni khedache.c: A good starting point for a tour of the ksour; be sure to stock up on water and fuel before hitting the dirt roads.

zaouia-mosquee sidi boulbaba (gabes).d: The Sidi Boulbaba Zaouia-Mosque Complex, dedicated to Abu Lubaba al-Ansari, a companion of the Prophet and the patron saint of Gabès. It houses the Gabès Ethnographic Museum.
zaouia-mosquee sidi boulbaba (gabes).a: A complex dedicated to Sidi Boulbaba, a companion of the Prophet and the patron saint of Gabès, which houses the ethnographic museum.
zaouia-mosquee sidi boulbaba (gabes).c: Dress appropriately; combine your visit with a tour of the adjacent ethnographic museum.

el hamma (gabes).d: A spa town located about 30 km west of Gabès, renowned since ancient times for its hot springs, which supply its hammams.
el hamma (gabes).a: A spa town renowned since ancient times for its hot springs, which feed the hammams.
el hamma (gabes).c: The hot springs are very hot: find out which pools are open to visitors.

ligne mareth.d: A system of fortifications in southern Tunisia built by France to face Italian-occupied Libya, captured by the Axis powers in 1942–1943. Breached by the British 8th Army in March 1943. Approximate coordinates.
ligne mareth.a: Remains of fortifications in southern Tunisia, breached by the British 8th Army in March 1943.
ligne mareth.c: Landmarks scattered across the plain: a guidebook or the Mareth Museum can help you locate them.

ouled el hadef (medina de tozeur).d: A historic district of Tozeur, famous for its clay-brick (toub) architecture featuring geometric relief patterns. A medieval medina.
ouled el hadef (medina de tozeur).a: A medieval neighborhood famous for its clay-brick (toub) facades featuring geometric relief patterns.
ouled el hadef (medina de tozeur).c: Stroll through the shaded alleyways on foot, preferably in the morning or late in the day.

ong jmel / mos espa (decor star wars).d: Abandoned Star Wars set near Nefta (Tozeur), the fictional spaceport of Mos Espa, near the Ong Jmel rock formation, which resembles a camel's neck.
ong jmel / mos espa (decor star wars).a: A Mos Espa movie set abandoned in the dunes, near the Ong Jmel rock formation shaped like a camel's neck.
ong jmel / mos espa (decor star wars).c: Access via a dirt track through the sand: a 4x4 is recommended, and come at sunrise or sunset for the best light.

kebili.d: The capital of the Kebili Governorate in the Nefzaoua region, one of the oldest oases in Tunisia and North Africa, near Chott el-Jerid. Deglet Nour dates.
kebili.a: The capital of Nefzaoua, one of the oldest oases in North Africa, located near Chott el-Jerid and renowned for its Deglet Nour dates.
kebili.c: A good base for exploring the Chott and the desert; intense heat in the summer.

ksar lemsa (limisa).d: A remarkably well-preserved 6th-century Byzantine fortress, situated amid the ruins of the ancient Roman-Berber city of Limisa. Located in Oueslatia (Kairouan), on the border with Siliana, it overlooks the valley with its nearly intact walls of large dressed stone.
ksar lemsa (limisa).a: A remarkably well-preserved 6th-century Byzantine fortress, with its nearly intact large-stone walls overlooking the valley, amid the ruins of Limisa.
ksar lemsa (limisa).c: Site on the outskirts of Siliana (Oueslatia area): You can explore the fortress in less than an hour, and it offers a beautiful view of the valley.

vicus maracitanus (ksar toual zammel).d: An ancient site in the Siliana Governorate, located about 15 km southwest of Siliana, identified as Vicus Maracitanus. A two-story Numidian-Roman mausoleum with a pilastered façade stands within its necropolis. It is linked to the question of the location of Zama.
vicus maracitanus (ksar toual zammel).a: A two-story Numidian-Roman mausoleum with a pilastered façade, located in the necropolises of this site associated with the Battle of Zama.
vicus maracitanus (ksar toual zammel).c: About 15 km southwest of Siliana; a rural site that requires precise coordinates to locate.

avitta bibba (henchir bou ftis).d: A Roman city in Africa Proconsularis near Bou Arada, north of Siliana (Henchir Bou Ftis). Former episcopal see; ruins of an amphitheater.
avitta bibba (henchir bou ftis).a: The scattered ruins of the Roman city, including the remains of an amphitheater, in the countryside near Bou Arada; a modest, largely undeveloped site.
avitta bibba (henchir bou ftis).c: For archaeology enthusiasts only; bring a car and ask locals for directions.

bisica lucana (henchir bichga).d: Roman city of Africa Proconsularis (Henchir Bichga, on the outskirts of Bou Arada, north of Siliana). Originally a colony, later a municipality: thermal baths, aqueduct, possible Capitol, former bishop’s seat. Approximate coordinates (Pleiades).
bisica lucana (henchir bichga).a: The scattered remains of the ancient Roman colony (thermal baths, traces of an aqueduct) in the countryside near Bou Arada; a modest site now in ruins.
bisica lucana (henchir bichga).c: A trail with few markers, best suited for experienced hikers; combine this hike with the nearby Avitta Bibba trail.

grande mosquee de nabeul.d: The Grand Mosque of Nabeul, designated a historic monument on March 3, 1915.
grande mosquee de nabeul.a: The Grand Mosque of Nabeul, designated a historic monument in 1915.
grande mosquee de nabeul.c: Sights to see while strolling through the medina of Nabeul; modest attire required.

mosquee sidi achour (nabeul).d: The Sidi Achour Mosque in Nabeul, designated a historic monument on March 3, 1915.
mosquee sidi achour (nabeul).a: The historic mosque in Nabeul, designated a historic monument in 1915.
mosquee sidi achour (nabeul).c: Mainly an outdoor tour; best combined with a stroll through the medina.

sanctuaire de thinissut.d: A Punic-Roman sanctuary dedicated to Baal Hammon and Tanit, located at Bir Bou Rekba near Hammamet. Terracotta statues at the Bardo.
sanctuaire de thinissut.a: A Punic-Roman sanctuary dedicated to Baal Hammon and Tanit, located at Bir Bou Rekba near Hammamet; its terracotta statues are housed in the Bardo Museum.
sanctuaire de thinissut.c: On site, the remains are sparse; the major statues can be seen at the Bardo Museum in Tunis.

temple capitolin de tubernuc.d: Ancient Capitoline Temple in Tubernuc (Soliman/Grombalia region), known locally as the great Byzantine monument with three doors.
temple capitolin de tubernuc.a: An ancient Capitoline Temple known locally as the "Great Monument with Three Gates," located in the Soliman/Grombalia area.
temple capitolin de tubernuc.c: This is a remote, undeveloped area; ask for directions when you arrive to find it.

musee dar khadija (hammamet).d: A museum housed in a traditional residence in Hammamet.
musee dar khadija (hammamet).a: A museum housed in a traditional Hammamet residence, showcasing local architecture and decorative arts.
musee dar khadija (hammamet).c: A short visit to combine with a tour of the medina in Hammamet.
musee dar khadija (hammamet).h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening hours on site.

missua (site antique de sidi daoud).d: Ancient archaeological site of Missua, in Sidi Daoud on Cap Bon. Low-precision Wikidata coordinates (~1 km), approximate.
missua (site antique de sidi daoud).a: Ancient Punic and Roman ruins at Sidi Daoud, on the northern coast of Cape Bon.
missua (site antique de sidi daoud).c: The location is hard to pinpoint and the site isn't very well showcased; best suited for enthusiasts.

hergla (horrea caelia).d: A small white coastal town on the Gulf of Hammamet, located on the site of the Roman town of Horrea Caelia. It features a medina with the Sidi Bou Mendil Mosque.
hergla (horrea caelia).a: the white village perched on the cliff; the Sidi Bou Mendil Mosque; the narrow streets overlooking the sea; and the old mat-weaving workshop.
hergla (horrea caelia).c: A picturesque stop between Sousse and Hammamet; a beautiful view of the sea from the edge of the plateau.

enfida (enfidaville).d: A city in the Sahel region near the ancient site of Uppenna. Museum of Early Christian mosaics; Commonwealth War Cemetery (1942–1943).
enfida (enfidaville).a: A city in the Sahel region near ancient Uppenna; home to a museum of early Christian mosaics and a Commonwealth military cemetery from the 1942–1943 campaign.
enfida (enfidaville).c: The Enfida Museum and the military cemetery are the two main attractions.

musee d'enfida.d: A former Neo-Romanesque church (1907) converted into a regional museum in 1966. It houses a rich collection of Christian funerary mosaics from Uppenna.
musee d'enfida.a: A former Neo-Romanesque church built in 1907 that has been converted into a regional museum, showcasing a rich collection of Christian funerary mosaics from Uppenna.
musee d'enfida.c: This is related to the nearby site of Uppenna, where the mosaics were found.
musee d'enfida.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening hours on site.

uppenna (henchir chigarnia).d: An ancient site north of Enfida featuring an early Christian basilica. The source of the famous epigraphic mosaics in the Enfida Museum.
uppenna (henchir chigarnia).a: An ancient site north of Enfida featuring an early Christian basilica, from which the famous epigraphic mosaics in the Enfida Museum originate.
uppenna (henchir chigarnia).c: A rather sparse site; the visit really comes into its own when combined with a visit to the Enfida Museum.

musee archeologique de sousse.d: A museum located in the Kasbah of Sousse, home to one of Tunisia's most extensive collections of Roman mosaics.
musee archeologique de sousse.a: Located in the kasbah, it houses one of the most extensive collections of Roman mosaics in Tunisia.
musee archeologique de sousse.c: A must-see in the Sahel for its mosaics; be sure to visit the kasbah that houses it as well.
musee archeologique de sousse.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening hours on site.

m'saken.d: A city in the Sahel region south of Sousse: the Great Mosque, the El Aousat Mosque, the Chakir Saheb Ettabaâ Palace (1828), and numerous zaouias.
m'saken.a: A city in the Sahel with a rich cultural heritage: the Great Mosque, the El Aousat Mosque, the Chakir Saheb Ettabaâ Palace (1828), and numerous zaouias.
m'saken.c: An urban walk off the beaten path; mostly outdoor sightseeing.

kalaa kebira.d: A city whose name means “great fortress.” Its historic center, “El Ksar,” was founded during the Aghlabid dynasty and was once surrounded by a rampart.
kalaa kebira.a: A city whose name means “great fortress,” centered around the old town of “El Ksar,” which was founded during the Aghlabid dynasty and was once surrounded by a rampart.
kalaa kebira.c: A nearby stop from Sousse for anyone interested in the historical fabric of the Sahel.

akouda.d: A town northwest of Sousse, known for the minaret of its Grand Mosque.
akouda.a: A town northwest of Sousse, known for the minaret of its Grand Mosque.
akouda.c: A brief stop; the main attractions are the minaret and the historic center.

synagogue de moknine.d: Former synagogue of the Jewish community of Moknine, a testament to Tunisia's Jewish heritage.
synagogue de moknine.a: Former synagogue of the Jewish community of Moknine, a testament to the Jewish-Tunisian heritage of the Sahel.
synagogue de moknine.c: Check with local authorities for visiting hours, as the building is not always open.

musee archeologique et ethnographique de.d: Museum of Punic artifacts and collections of folk art and traditions (textiles, jewelry, crafts). Opened in 2007.
musee archeologique et ethnographique de.a: Museum (2007) featuring a mix of Punic artifacts and collections of folk art and traditions: textiles, jewelry, and local crafts.
musee archeologique et ethnographique de.c: A good overview of the material culture of the Sahel; worth seeing along with the Moknine synagogue.
musee archeologique et ethnographique de.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening hours on site.

musee des arts et traditions populaires.d: Monastir Museum of Folk Arts and Traditions, located in the medina (founded in 1985).
musee des arts et traditions populaires.a: Museum of Folk Arts and Traditions located in the medina of Monastir (founded in 1985).
musee des arts et traditions populaires.c: A visit to include as part of a Medina-Ribat tour of Monastir.
musee des arts et traditions populaires.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening hours on site.

remparts de monastir.d: The ancient walls of the medina of Monastir, distinct from the ribat.
remparts de monastir.a: The ancient walls of the medina of Monastir, separate from the ribat, marking the city's historic layout.
remparts de monastir.c: Discover this as you stroll through the medina during your visit to the ribat.

mausolee omar makhlouf (monastir).d: Zaouïa and mausoleum in the medina of Monastir, a traditional place of worship.
mausolee omar makhlouf (monastir).a: The Zaouïa and mausoleum in the medina of Monastir, a traditional place of worship.
mausolee omar makhlouf (monastir).c: A small building worth seeing as you walk through the medina; please respect the sacred nature of the site.

ruspina.d: An ancient Punic and later Roman city corresponding to present-day Monastir, mentioned in ancient sources (Caesar's Civil War).
ruspina.a: An ancient Punic and later Roman city corresponding to present-day Monastir, mentioned in ancient sources (Caesar's Civil War); very few remains.
ruspina.c: More of a historical landmark than a site open to visitors, as the modern city has built over the ancient one.

tataouine (foum tataouine).d: The capital of the Tataouine Governorate, a former garrison town during the Protectorate era, and the gateway to the ksour of Dahar.
tataouine (foum tataouine).a: A former garrison town of the Protectorate, serving as the gateway to the ksours of Dahar.
tataouine (foum tataouine).c: Starting point for tours to the ksour: Make sure to fill up on water and fuel.

ksar ouled aoun.d: A semi-circular ksar with ghorfas near Maztouria, ranging from 96 to 220 ghorfas spread over two to three stories; restored in 2007.
ksar ouled aoun.a: A restored, semicircular ksar a ghorfas near Maztouria, with two to three stories.
ksar ouled aoun.c: A short stop; the light at the end of the day is the most flattering for photos.

ksar el kedim.d: Fortified ksar in the Tataouine Governorate, a designated historic site attributed to the Zenete Berbers.
ksar el kedim.a: A listed fortified ksar, believed to have been built by the Zenete Berbers, in the Tataouine Governorate.
ksar el kedim.c: A modest site to include on a tour of the ksour with a local guide.

ksar dghaghra.d: A Berber ksar (fortified granary) in the Tataouine Governorate.
ksar dghaghra.a: A Berber ksar (fortified granary) in the Tataouine Governorate.
ksar dghaghra.c: A quick visit; can be combined with a tour of the neighboring ksours of Dahar.

ksar jelidet (ksar boujlida).d: Ksar of the Ksour Jelidet complex, a listed Berber fort-granary.
ksar jelidet (ksar boujlida).a: A listed Berber granary fortress, part of the Ksour Jelidet complex.
ksar jelidet (ksar boujlida).c: Access via trails: A local guide makes it easier to find your way.

ksar beni ghedir.d: Ksar a Ghorfas in the northern part of the Tataouine Governorate, in the area of the fortified granaries of Dahar.
ksar beni ghedir.a: Ksar a Ghorfas, north of Tataouine, in the area of the fortified granaries of Dahar.
ksar beni ghedir.c: A short stop; to be included in a tour of the ksour.

ksar beni mhira (el ataya).d: A rectangular ksar (150x70 m) on a hill in the Djeffara region, with approximately 160 ghorfas.
ksar beni mhira (el ataya).a: A rectangular ksar (150x70 m) on a hill in the Djeffara region, with approximately 160 ghorfas.
ksar beni mhira (el ataya).c: A pleasant vantage point for watching the sunset; bring water.

ksar beni mhira (zorgane).d: A parallelogram-shaped ksar (120x80 m) near Beni Mhira, with 170 to 250 ghorfas on two stories.
ksar beni mhira (zorgane).a: A parallelogram-shaped ksar (120 x 80 m) with 170 to 250 ghorfas on two stories.
ksar beni mhira (zorgane).c: Best visited in conjunction with the other ksar, Beni Mhira; expect hot weather.

remada (tillibari).d: A southern city near the Libyan border, located on the site of the ancient Roman fort of Tillibari (Limes).
remada (tillibari).a: A city in the south located on the site of the ancient Roman fort of Tillibari (Limes), near the Libyan border.
remada (tillibari).c: Remote border area: Find out about access and bring water with you.

dehiba.d: A city in the eastern part of the Tataouine Governorate, serving as a border crossing with Libya.
dehiba.a: A city east of Tataouine, serving as a border crossing with Libya.
dehiba.c: Mainly of interest for transit; check the conditions in the border area.

medenine (ville et ksour).d: The capital of the Medenine Governorate, famous for its ksour a ghorfas (collective stores of the Berber tribes).
medenine (ville et ksour).a: A regional capital famous for its ksour a ghorfas, ancient communal storehouses of the Berber tribes.
medenine (ville et ksour).c: A few restored ghorfas are open to visitors in town; a convenient stopover on the way to the ksour of Dahar.

zarzis (gergis).d: A coastal town in the southeast, a seaside resort surrounded by olive groves, located on the site of ancient Gergis.
zarzis (gergis).a: A seaside resort surrounded by olive groves, located on the site of ancient Gergis.
zarzis (gergis).c: Beaches and coastal relaxation; can be combined with a trip to nearby Djerba.

ben gardane.d: A city in the southeast near the Libyan border, and a major cross-border trade hub.
ben gardane.a: A city in the southeast, a major cross-border commercial hub near Libya.
ben gardane.c: Mainly of commercial and transit interest; check for the latest news regarding the border area.

ajim (djerba).d: A coastal town on the western side of Djerba, the main ferry crossing to the mainland, and a former sponge-fishing port.
ajim (djerba).a: The western port of Djerba, the main ferry link to the mainland and a former sponge-fishing port.
ajim (djerba).c: The ferry connecting Djerba to the mainland: expect delays during rush hour.

sedouikech (djerba).d: A village in central Djerba, one of the few places where the Djerba Berber language is still spoken.
sedouikech (djerba).a: A village in central Djerba, one of the few places on the island where the Berber language is still spoken.
sedouikech (djerba).c: A peaceful retreat in the heart of the island, far from the hustle and bustle of the beach.

midoun (djerba).d: The second-largest city in Djerba in terms of population, located in the northeastern part of the island.
midoun (djerba).a: The second-largest city on Djerba, a bustling hub in the northeastern part of the island.
midoun (djerba).c: Popular weekly walk: Come early to enjoy the atmosphere and beat the heat.

mahboubine (djerba).d: A village in southeastern Djerba, known for its Ottoman-inspired El Kateb Mosque.
mahboubine (djerba).a: A village in southeastern Djerba, known for its Ottoman-inspired El Kateb Mosque.
mahboubine (djerba).c: A quick stop to admire the mosque; please dress appropriately when visiting.

el kantara (djerba).d: A town in southeastern Djerba, located along the Roman road connecting the island to the mainland near Zarzis.
el kantara (djerba).a: A town located on the site of the Roman road connecting the island to the mainland near Zarzis.
el kantara (djerba).c: Road crossing: a convenient way to reach the mainland.

boughrara.d: A village on the mainland near the ancient city of Gightis, on the coast facing Djerba.
boughrara.a: A coastal village on the mainland, near the ancient city of Gightis, across from Djerba.
boughrara.c: Combine this with a visit to the nearby ancient site of Gightis.

medina de gabes (jara).d: The historic heart of Gabès, an oasis city on the gulf, and the old neighborhoods of Petite and Grande Jara, located on the site of ancient Tacapae.
medina de gabes (jara).a: The historic heart of the oasis city on the gulf, featuring the old neighborhoods of Petite Jara and Grande Jara, on the site of ancient Tacapae.
medina de gabes (jara).c: Stroll through the medina and the nearby oasis, avoiding the midday heat.

ghannouch.d: A municipality and administrative district of the Gabès Governorate, located on the gulf north of the city.
ghannouch.a: A municipality in the Gulf of Gabès, north of the city.
ghannouch.c: Ordinary destination: of limited interest to visitors; more of a stopover.

oudhref.d: A town and administrative district in the Gabès Governorate, northwest of Gabès.
oudhref.a: A town and administrative district in the northwest of Gabès.
oudhref.c: A stopover; not of major tourist interest.

el metouia.d: An Oasian settlement and a branch office of the Gabès Governorate, located north of the city.
el metouia.a: An oasis town north of Gabès, in the Gulf Oasis.
el metouia.c: A cool stroll under the palm trees is possible during the hottest part of the day.

nouvelle matmata.d: A new town built on the Aradh Plateau to resettle the Berber populations from the Matmata Mountains.
nouvelle matmata.a: A new town built on the Aradh Plateau to resettle the Berbers from the Matmata Mountains.
nouvelle matmata.c: A stop on the way to historic Matmata and its cave dwellings.

chenini nahal (gabes).d: A village and coastal oasis southwest of Gabès (date palms, henna). Distinct from the Berber village of Chenini in Tataouine.
chenini nahal (gabes).a: A village and coastal oasis southwest of Gabès (date palms, henna); distinct from the Berber village of Chenini in Tataouine.
chenini nahal (gabes).c: A shaded stroll through the oasis; not to be confused with Chenini in Tataouine.

mareth.d: A town between Gabès and Medenine, which gave its name to the Mareth Line (1930s).
mareth.a: A town that gave its name to the Mareth Line; a local museum commemorates the 1943 battle.
mareth.c: The Mareth Line Museum helps visitors understand the surrounding ruins.

zarat.d: A coastal town in the Gabès Governorate, south of Gabès, with a fishing port.
zarat.a: A coastal town south of Gabès, with a fishing port.
zarat.c: Small-town port atmosphere; mainly of local interest.

bataille de l'oued akarit.d: A battle during the Tunisian campaign along the Akarit Wadi, north of Gabès, in the area between the sea and the chotts.
bataille de l'oued akarit.a: A memorial to the Battle of April 1943, located in the area between the sea and the chotts north of Gabès.
bataille de l'oued akarit.c: A memorial site with no significant landscaping: of primarily historical interest.

bouchemma.d: A town and municipality in the Gabès Governorate (Western Gabès), located in the Gabès Oasis.
bouchemma.a: A town in the Gabès Oasis (West Gabès).
bouchemma.c: A quiet stop in the oasis; not much of a tourist attraction.

el guettar.d: An oasis town southeast of Gafsa, famous for the El Guettar Hermaion (Mousterian/Aterian) and the Battle of El Guettar (1943).
el guettar.a: An oasis town famous for the El Guettar Hermaion (Mousterian/Aterian) and the battle of 1943.
el guettar.c: The prehistoric context can be better understood by visiting the nearby Gafsa Museum.

metlaoui.d: A mining town in the Gafsa Basin (phosphate), the starting point of the Lezard Rouge train bound for the Selja Gorges.
metlaoui.a: A mining town in the Gafsa Basin and the starting point of the Lezard Rouge train to the Selja Gorges.
metlaoui.c: Book Lezard Rouge in advance; water is essential in the summer.

redeyef.d: A phosphate mining town in the Gafsa Basin, the epicenter of the 2008 social movement.
redeyef.a: A phosphate mining town in the Gafsa Basin, the epicenter of the 2008 social movement.
redeyef.c: Of primarily historical and social interest; a stop on the Lezard Rouge line.

moulares (oum el araies).d: A phosphate mining town (Oum El Araies) located about 50 km from Gafsa, near the Algerian border.
moulares (oum el araies).a: A phosphate mining town located about 50 km from Gafsa, near the Algerian border.

mdhilla.d: A phosphate mining town in the Gafsa Governorate (CPG plant).
mdhilla.a: A phosphate mining town in the Gafsa Governorate, home to the CPG plant.
mdhilla.c: Industrial town: not very interesting for visitors.

sened.d: A village and the seat of the delegation, located about 50 km east of Gafsa, known for its ancient Berber dialect.
sened.a: A village about 50 km east of Gafsa, known for its ancient Berber dialect.
sened.c: A quiet stop; of interest mainly for its culture and language.

belkhir.d: A town and the administrative center of the Gafsa Governorate.
belkhir.a: Administrative seat of the Gafsa Governorate.
belkhir.c: Stopover: not of major tourist interest.

sidi aich.d: A town and the seat of the delegation north of Gafsa, in a region characterized by mountainous terrain and mountain oases.
sidi aich.a: A town north of Gafsa, in a region of mountainous terrain and mountain oases.
sidi aich.c: A possible starting point for trips to the surrounding mountain oases.

degache.d: An oasis town in the Jerid region north of Tozeur, on the edge of Chott el-Jerid (deglet nour).
degache.a: An oasis town in the Jerid region on the edge of Chott el-Jerid, renowned for its Deglet Nour dates.
degache.c: A walk toward the chott; a stroll through the palm grove during the cooler hours of the day.

hazoua.d: A small oasis town in the Tozeur Governorate, near the Algerian border.
hazoua.a: A small oasis town near the Algerian border, in the governorate of Tozeur.
hazoua.c: Remote border town: Be sure to bring water and fuel.

blidet.d: An oasis village in the Kebili Governorate, in the Nefzaoua Oasis region.
blidet.a: The oasis village of Nefzaoua, in the Kebili oasis region.
blidet.c: A peaceful oasis; the shade of the palm trees is a welcome respite in the summer.

jemna.d: An oasis town in the Nefzaoua region, renowned for its springs and date production; it features an old mosque with an ancient library.
jemna.a: An oasis town in the Nefzaoua region, renowned for its springs and dates, featuring an old mosque with an ancient library.
jemna.c: A walk through the palm grove; intense heat in the summer.

zaafrane.d: An oasis village in the Kebili Governorate, the gateway to the Grand Erg Oriental and the center of the Adhara nomads.
zaafrane.a: An oasis village, the gateway to the Grand Erg Oriental and the center of the Adhara nomads.
zaafrane.c: Departure for excursions in the dunes: 4x4 or camel ride at sunrise/sunset.

sabria.d: An oasis village in the Kebili Governorate, nestled among the first major dunes, about 30 km from Douz.
sabria.a: This oasis village is nestled among the first major dunes, about 30 km from Douz.
sabria.c: Saharan landscape: Come admire the dunes bathed in the low morning or evening light.

el faouar.d: A city and the administrative center of the Kebili Governorate, located in a Saharan oasis.
el faouar.a: An oasis town in the Sahara, the administrative center of the Kebili Governorate.
el faouar.c: Starting point for the desert; extreme heat in the summer—leave early.

souk lahad.d: An oasis town and the administrative center of the Nefzaoua delegation, located about 15 km northwest of Kebili, on the edge of Chott el-Jerid.
souk lahad.a: An oasis town in the Nefzaoua region, on the edge of Chott el-Jerid, about 15 km from Kebili.
souk lahad.c: Oasis stop; combine with a crossing of the chott.

telmine.d: The village of North Kebili, on the edge of Chott el-Jerid, near the ancient site of Turris Tamalleni.
telmine.a: A village on the edge of Chott el-Jerid, near the ancient site of Turris Tamalleni.
telmine.c: Combine this with a visit to the nearby ruins of Turris Tamalleni.

turris tamalleni (telmine).d: An ancient site near Telmine, at the western end of the Limes Tripolitanus: a Roman fort that later became a municipality under Hadrian, and the center of the Nybgenii tribe.
turris tamalleni (telmine).a: An ancient site at the western end of the Limes: a Roman fort that became a municipality under Hadrian, and the center of the Nybgenii tribe.
turris tamalleni (telmine).c: Modest open-air ruins: a guide helps interpret them; bring water and a hat.

fatnassa.d: An oasis village in the Souk Lahad district, on the southern shore of Chott el-Jerid.
fatnassa.a: An oasis village on the southern shore of Chott el-Jerid, in the Souk Lahad district.
fatnassa.c: A peaceful oasis-like stop; the shade of the palm trees is welcome in the summer.

centenarium tibubuci (ksar tarcine).d: Late Roman fort on the edge of the Grand Erg Oriental, part of the Limes Tripolitanus. UNESCO Tentative List.
centenarium tibubuci (ksar tarcine).a: Late Roman fort (circa 297–305) on the edge of the Grand Erg Oriental, part of the Limes; on the UNESCO Tentative List.
centenarium tibubuci (ksar tarcine).c: Access via the Saharan trail: A 4x4 vehicle and a guide are required, and you’ll need plenty of water.

bordj lazarit (ghar el melh).d: The Ottoman fort at Ghar el Melh, one of the three bordjs near the ancient port of Porto Farina.
bordj lazarit (ghar el melh).a: The third of the 17th-century Ottoman forts at Ghar el Melh, near the ancient port of Porto Farina.
bordj lazarit (ghar el melh).c: Complete your tour of the three bordjs; allow half a day to explore the entire site and the lagoon.

pont mobile de bizerte.d: An iconic bascule bridge spanning the Bizerte Canal, connecting the city to Zarzouna.
pont mobile de bizerte.a: The 1980 bascule bridge spanning the Bizerte Canal and connecting the city to Zarzouna is an iconic feature of the urban landscape.
pont mobile de bizerte.c: An interesting sight to watch from the docks, especially when the locks are raised to allow ships to pass through.

mosquee rebaa (bizerte).d: Historic Mosque in the Medina of Bizerte.
mosquee rebaa (bizerte).a: A historic Ottoman-era mosque in the heart of the medina of Bizerte.
mosquee rebaa (bizerte).c: Appropriate attire is required; best seen while strolling through the medina, as there is no designated tour route.

zaouia sidi el arbi (ras jebel).d: Zaouïa and mausoleum in Ras Jebel, a local place of worship.
zaouia sidi el arbi (ras jebel).a: The zaouia and mausoleum of Sidi El Arbi in Ras Jebel, a site of local worship.
zaouia sidi el arbi (ras jebel).c: A small place of worship: a brief visit, best combined with a tour of the Andalusian coastal villages (Raf Raf, Metline).

musee oceanographique de bizerte.d: Museum of Marine Fauna and Flora, near the Old Port of Bizerte.
musee oceanographique de bizerte.a: The collections of Mediterranean marine flora and fauna, on display near the old port.
musee oceanographique de bizerte.c: A short, sheltered tour, ideal for bad weather; best combined with a stroll through the Old Port.
musee oceanographique de bizerte.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening hours on site.

musee national d'utique.d: Archaeological Museum of the Punic and Roman Ruins at the Site of Utica.
musee national d'utique.a: The Punic and Roman archaeological collections from the site of Utica: artifacts, sculptures, and mosaics.
musee national d'utique.c: Best visited just before or after the nearby site of Utica; allow about 1 hour.
musee national d'utique.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening hours on site.

ecomusee de l'ichkeul.d: Ichkeul National Park Ecomuseum (fauna, flora, geology), at the foot of Djebel Ichkeul.
ecomusee de l'ichkeul.a: Presentations on the flora, fauna, and geology of Ichkeul National Park, at the foot of Djebel Ichkeul.
ecomusee de l'ichkeul.c: The ideal starting point for a visit to the park; start here to get a sense of the site before climbing the djebel.
ecomusee de l'ichkeul.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening hours on site.

maison de la cascade (utique).d: Roman domus at the Utica site, decorated with mosaics and featuring a pool.
maison de la cascade (utique).a: The Roman domus, adorned with mosaics and featuring a pool, is one of the most beautiful residential complexes at the Utica site.
maison de la cascade (utique).c: Included in the tour of the Utica site; take a look at the mosaics still in place around the pool.

eglise saint-alexandre-nevski de bizerte.d: Russian Orthodox Church in Bizerte, built by sailors from the Russian fleet who took refuge there after 1920.
eglise saint-alexandre-nevski de bizerte.a: The Russian Orthodox church built in 1939 by sailors from the Russian fleet who had taken refuge in Bizerte after 1920.
eglise saint-alexandre-nevski de bizerte.c: A small, unique building in the city; a quick visit, best combined with a tour of downtown Bizerte.

sejnane.d: A rural town known for its pottery, which is hand-shaped by women, and was inscribed on the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage List in 2018.
sejnane.a: The craft of hand-molded pottery made by women, inscribed on UNESCO’s Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2018, and the town’s rural atmosphere.
sejnane.c: Visit pottery workshops and cooperatives to view and purchase traditional ceramics; combine this with a visit to the nearby wetlands.

raf raf.d: A coastal town famous for its beach and its Andalusian heritage, facing Pilau Island.
raf raf.a: The large beach facing Pilau Island and the Andalusian heritage of this coastal town.
raf raf.c: Above all, a beach getaway: plan your visit for the warmer months and combine it with a trip to nearby Cape Sidi Ali El Mekki.

metline.d: A coastal village of Andalusian origin northeast of Bizerte (known for its maritime and wine-growing heritage).
metline.a: The coastal village of Andalusian origin northeast of Bizerte, with its maritime and wine-growing heritage.
metline.c: A peaceful stop to combine with a visit to Raf Raf and the other Andalusian villages along the coast.

el alia.d: A town of Andalusian origin known for its chechia craftsmanship and textile traditions.
el alia.a: The Andalusian city renowned for its chechia craftsmanship and textile traditions.
el alia.c: Discover the chechia workshops; a short visit that can be combined with visits to other Andalusian towns in the region.

petite mosquee de beja.d: The historic mosque in the medina of Beja, which is more modest than the Great Mosque.
petite mosquee de beja.a: A historic mosque, more modest than the Great Mosque, located in the heart of the medina of Béja.
petite mosquee de beja.c: Worth seeing while strolling through the medina; proper attire required.

eglise notre-dame-du-rosaire de beja.d: A Catholic church built during the Protectorate era in Beja.
eglise notre-dame-du-rosaire de beja.a: The Catholic church, built during the Protectorate era, stands as a testament to Béja's colonial heritage.
eglise notre-dame-du-rosaire de beja.c: A quick stop in the city center—a must-see when exploring Béja.

chaouach (sua).d: A hilltop village on the site of ancient Sua, dominated by a Byzantine fortress and featuring Roman and Christian ruins. North of Teboursouk.
chaouach (sua).a: The hilltop village of ancient Sua, dominated by a Byzantine fortress, with Roman and Christian ruins.
chaouach (sua).c: Mountain trail north of Teboursouk: best combined with a visit to nearby Toukabeur; wear sturdy shoes for the climb.

toukabeur (thuccabor).d: A village perched atop ancient Thuccabor, featuring Roman ruins and an old mosque. A heritage site along with Chaouach.
toukabeur (thuccabor).a: The village perched atop ancient Thuccabor, with its Roman ruins and historic mosque, forms a heritage duo with Chaouach.
toukabeur (thuccabor).c: Combine this with Chaouach on the same trip; be sure to bring a vehicle suitable for mountain roads.

teboursouk.d: A historic town that was once the ancient Thubursicum Bure (medina, kasbah, ramparts), serving as the gateway to Dougga.
teboursouk.a: The historic city of ancient Thubursicum Bure: medina, kasbah, and ramparts—the gateway to Dougga.
teboursouk.c: A convenient stop before or after Dougga; make it a stopover for services and to visit the medina.

musee de teboursouk.d: Archaeological museum housing collections from the region's ancient sites, notably Dougga.
musee de teboursouk.a: Archaeological collections from the region's ancient sites, notably Dougga.
musee de teboursouk.c: A short side trip to complement the visit to Dougga; check for opening hours on site.
musee de teboursouk.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening hours on site.

mosquee de bab teboursouk (testour).d: The Andalusian-style Testour Mosque, near the Teboursouk Gate, a legacy of the Moriscos.
mosquee de bab teboursouk (testour).a: The Andalusian-style mosque near the Teboursouk Gate, part of Testour's Moorish heritage.
mosquee de bab teboursouk (testour).c: A must-see during a stroll through Testour, along with the Great Andalusian Mosque; proper attire is required.

zaouia sidi naceur (testour).d: The Zaouïa and mausoleum of the saint Sidi Naceur in Testour, a legacy of Andalusian heritage.
zaouia sidi naceur (testour).a: The zaouia and mausoleum of the saint Sidi Naceur, a testament to Testour's Andalusian heritage.
zaouia sidi naceur (testour).c: A brief stop to explore along with the other Andalusian monuments in Testour.

medjez el-bab.d: A strategic town on the Medjerda River, a historic crossing point, and a key location in the Tunisian Campaign (1942–1943).
medjez el-bab.a: The strategic city on the Medjerda River, its historic crossing point, and traces of the 1942–1943 Tunisian Campaign.
medjez el-bab.c: Combine this with a visit to the Ottoman Bridge and the Commonwealth Memorial; a stop to learn about military and river history.

memorial de medjez el-bab.d: Commonwealth Memorial honoring the soldiers who went missing during the Tunisian campaign and have no known grave.
memorial de medjez el-bab.a: The Commonwealth Memorial honoring the soldiers who went missing in action and have no known grave from the Tunisian campaign.
memorial de medjez el-bab.c: A place for reflection; a quiet, brief visit, best combined with a visit to the bridge and the town of Medjez el-Bab.

nefza.d: A town in the northwestern part of the Beja Governorate, a forested and mountainous region near Kroumirie.
nefza.a: The forested and mountainous landscape of the northwestern part of the Béja Governorate, at the gateway to the Kroumirie region.
nefza.c: Above all, a nature-focused stop: best enjoyed in spring, along with Djebel Khroufa and the surrounding forests.

theatre de bulla regia.d: Roman theater at the Bulla Regia archaeological site, near Jendouba.
theatre de bulla regia.a: The Roman theater at the Bulla Regia site, whose tiers and orchestra are still visible.
theatre de bulla regia.c: Included in the tour of Bulla Regia; be sure to check it out as you explore the entire site.

thermes de julia memmia (bulla regia).d: The Great Public Baths of Bulla Regia (2nd century), among the city's most impressive monuments.
thermes de julia memmia (bulla regia).a: The large public baths dating from the 2nd century, which are among the most imposing monuments in Bulla Regia thanks to their well-preserved walls and vaults.
thermes de julia memmia (bulla regia).c: The highlight of a visit to Bulla Regia is looking up at the tall structures that are still standing.

maison d'amphitrite (bulla regia).d: Underground residence in Bulla Regia, famous for its Amphitrite mosaic. Cave architecture.
maison d'amphitrite (bulla regia).a: The underground dwelling, famous for its Amphitrite mosaic, which remains in place, is a remarkable example of the troglodytic dwellings of Bulla Regia.
maison d'amphitrite (bulla regia).c: Go down into the underground room to admire the mosaic, which is cooler during the hottest part of the day; don't miss it.

maison de la chasse (bulla regia).d: A semi-subterranean Roman residence in Bulla Regia, decorated with mosaics, typical of underground dwellings.
maison de la chasse (bulla regia).a: The semi-subterranean Roman residence adorned with mosaics, typical of the underground dwellings at Bulla Regia.
maison de la chasse (bulla regia).c: Be sure to visit the neighboring House of Amphitrite as part of your tour of the underground villas.

temple d'apollon (bulla regia).d: Roman temple dedicated to Apollo in Bulla Regia; the statues are now in the Bardo Museum.
temple d'apollon (bulla regia).a: The ruins of the temple dedicated to Apollo, whose statues are now housed in the Bardo Museum.
temple d'apollon (bulla regia).c: A stop on the Bulla Regia tour; for the statues, extend your visit to the Bardo in Tunis.

musee de bulla regia.d: A site museum displaying artifacts and mosaics from the excavations at Bulla Regia.
musee de bulla regia.a: Artifacts and mosaics from the excavations at Bulla Regia, on display at the site museum.
musee de bulla regia.c: A good place to visit in addition to the archaeological site; allow about half an hour.
musee de bulla regia.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening hours on site.

theatre de chemtou (simitthus).d: Roman theater of ancient Simitthus (Chemtou), on the banks of the Medjerda River.
theatre de chemtou (simitthus).a: The Roman theater of ancient Simitthus, on the banks of the Medjerda River.
theatre de chemtou (simitthus).c: Included in the Chemtou tour; to be visited along with the quarries and the museum.

basilique de chemtou.d: The Roman civil basilica of Simitthus, in the heart of the ancient city.
basilique de chemtou.a: The Roman civil basilica in the heart of the ancient city of Simitthus.
basilique de chemtou.c: A stop on the Chemtou trail; to be visited in conjunction with the nearby theater and Roman bridge.

musee de chemtou.d: Archaeological Museum of Numidian Marble and the Ruins of Simitthus (marble quarries).
musee de chemtou.a: The museum dedicated to Numidian yellow marble and the ruins of Simitthus, which explains how the quarries were operated by the Romans.
musee de chemtou.c: Start at the museum to get a sense of the site, then explore the quarries; combine this with a visit to Bulla Regia.
musee de chemtou.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening hours on site.

musee de la memoire commune tuniso-alger.d: The Ghardimaou Museum, dedicated to the shared history of Tunisia and Algeria (the struggle for independence).
musee de la memoire commune tuniso-alger.a: The collections dedicated to the shared history of Tunisia and Algeria and to the struggle for independence, in Ghardimaou.
musee de la memoire commune tuniso-alger.c: Historical-themed tour near the border; best combined with a visit to the nearby Ain Zana Nature Reserve.
musee de la memoire commune tuniso-alger.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening hours on site.

cimetiere militaire de ras rajel.d: Commonwealth Military Cemetery near Tabarka (soldiers from the Tunisian Campaign).
cimetiere militaire de ras rajel.a: The Commonwealth military cemetery, where soldiers who fought in the Tunisian campaign are buried, is located in a well-maintained setting near Tabarka.
cimetiere militaire de ras rajel.c: A peaceful place of remembrance; a brief stop on the way to Tabarka, to be approached with respect.

henchir-bez.d: Ancient archaeological site (henchir) in the northwestern part of the Kairouan Governorate.
henchir-bez.a: An ancient archaeological site (Henchir) in the northwestern part of the Kairouan Governorate; modest remains.
henchir-bez.c: Mainly of archaeological interest: Check with local authorities for access information.

el aouja (site de ceramique sigillee).d: An ancient archaeological site known as the place where sigillata pottery was discovered.
el aouja (site de ceramique sigillee).a: An ancient site known for the discovery of sigillata pottery; the surface remains are not particularly spectacular.

necropole de haouch taacha.d: Roman necropolis in the southern part of the Kairouan Governorate.
necropole de haouch taacha.a: Roman necropolis in the southern part of the Kairouan Governorate.
necropole de haouch taacha.c: The location is hard to spot: make sure to have someone help you find it.

pont-aqueduc sur l'oued cherchira.d: An old aqueduct bridge spanning the Cherchira wadi, near Haffouz.
pont-aqueduc sur l'oued cherchira.a: An old hydraulic structure spanning the Cherchira wadi, near Haffouz.
pont-aqueduc sur l'oued cherchira.c: Worth checking out if you're traveling through the Haffouz region.

pont romain sur l'oued djilf.d: Roman bridge spanning the Djilf Wadi, Oueslatia region.
pont romain sur l'oued djilf.a: Roman bridge spanning the Djilf wadi, in the Oueslatia region.
pont romain sur l'oued djilf.c: A short stop for fans of Roman architecture, by car.

mausolee sidi amor abbada.d: Sidi Amor Abbada Zaouia (Mosque of the Sabres), 19th century, recognizable by its five fluted domes.
mausolee sidi amor abbada.a: A 19th-century zaouia known as the "Mosque of the Sabres," recognizable by its five fluted domes and monumental features.
mausolee sidi amor abbada.c: Points of interest to include on a walk through Kairouan; appropriate attire is appreciated.

mausolee el ouhaichia.d: Zaouia-mausoleum in the medina of Kairouan.
mausolee el ouhaichia.a: The Zaouïa-mausoleum in the medina of Kairouan; a modest monument.
mausolee el ouhaichia.c: Things to see while strolling through the medina.

mausolee sidi abdesselam.d: Zaouia-mausoleum in the medina of Kairouan.
mausolee sidi abdesselam.a: The Zaouïa-mausoleum in the medina of Kairouan; a modest monument.
mausolee sidi abdesselam.c: Things to see while strolling through the medina.

mosquee al malek (kairouan).d: Historic mosque in the medina of Kairouan.
mosquee al malek (kairouan).a: Historic mosque in the medina of Kairouan.
mosquee al malek (kairouan).c: Place of worship: Observe from the outside and be discreet.

mosquee sikaya (kairouan).d: Historic mosque in the medina of Kairouan.
mosquee sikaya (kairouan).a: Historic mosque in the medina of Kairouan.
mosquee sikaya (kairouan).c: Place of worship: Observe from the outside and be discreet.

mosquee el lawlib (kairouan).d: Historic mosque in the medina of Kairouan.
mosquee el lawlib (kairouan).a: Historic mosque in the medina of Kairouan.
mosquee el lawlib (kairouan).c: Place of worship: Observe from the outside and be discreet.

eglise de l'immaculee-conception de kair.d: The Catholic Church in Kairouan, a legacy of the French Protectorate.
eglise de l'immaculee-conception de kair.a: A Catholic church inherited from the French protectorate, a testament to the city's colonial heritage.
eglise de l'immaculee-conception de kair.c: Please check on site before visiting, as the building is not always open.

musee du tapis de kairouan.d: A museum dedicated to Kairouan carpets, located in the medina.
musee du tapis de kairouan.a: A museum dedicated to Kairouan carpets, a craft that is emblematic of the city.
musee du tapis de kairouan.c: A nice way to round off the day before heading out to visit the weavers' workshops in the medina.
musee du tapis de kairouan.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening hours on site.

camp de concentration de kondas.d: Former concentration camp in Kondas, Kairouan Governorate.
camp de concentration de kondas.a: Site of a former World War II concentration camp; a memorial site with no notable remnants.
camp de concentration de kondas.c: A memorial site rather than a tourist attraction; check with local sources for more information.

musee de mahdia.d: Mahdia Archaeological and Ethnographic Museum, separate from Borj el-Kebir.
musee de mahdia.a: Mahdia Archaeological and Ethnographic Museum (1997), showcasing the history of the city and its region.
musee de mahdia.c: Combine this with a visit to the medina and Borj el-Kebir.
musee de mahdia.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening hours on site.

dar sghir (mahdia).d: A museum housed in a traditional house in the medina of Mahdia.
dar sghir (mahdia).a: A small museum housed in a traditional house in the medina, showcasing local architecture and arts.
dar sghir (mahdia).c: A quick stop during a stroll through the medina.

musee archeologique de salakta.d: The Salakta Archaeological Museum, which displays the ruins of ancient Sullecthum.
musee archeologique de salakta.a: A museum displaying the ruins of ancient Sullecthum, including a large mosaic depicting a lion.
musee archeologique de salakta.c: Be sure to visit the nearby archaeological site of Salakta.
musee archeologique de salakta.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening hours on site.

cimetiere marin de mahdia.d: A seaside cemetery on the Mahdia Peninsula, overlooking the sea.
cimetiere marin de mahdia.a: A historic cemetery overlooking the sea on the Mahdia Peninsula; a peaceful setting along the coast.
cimetiere marin de mahdia.c: A place of contemplation: Please visit with respect, especially at sunrise or sunset.

eglise notre-dame-du-mont-carmel de mahd.d: The Catholic Church in Mahdia, dating from the colonial era.
eglise notre-dame-du-mont-carmel de mahd.a: A Catholic church from the colonial era, a testament to Mahdia's diverse history.
eglise notre-dame-du-mont-carmel de mahd.c: Irregular opening hours: Please check on site.

phare de mahdia (cap afrique).d: Lighthouse at the tip of the Mahdia Peninsula (Cap Afrique).
phare de mahdia (cap afrique).a: A lighthouse at the tip of the peninsula (Cap Afrique), a navigational landmark offering views of the coastline.
phare de mahdia (cap afrique).c: A beautiful walk to the tip; access to the interior may be restricted.

phare de chebba.d: Chebba Lighthouse, near Cape Ras Kapoudia.
phare de chebba.a: A lighthouse near Cape Ras Kapoudia, on the rocky coastline of the Sahel.
phare de chebba.c: Coastal viewpoint: Approach from the coast, as access to the lighthouse itself may be limited.

grand chapiteau corinthien (el jem).d: A large ancient Corinthian capital among the Roman ruins of Thysdrus in El Jem.
grand chapiteau corinthien (el jem).a: A large ancient Corinthian capital among the scattered ruins of Thysdrus in El Jem.
grand chapiteau corinthien (el jem).c: A detail to look out for when visiting the Roman ruins at El Jem.

second amphitheatre d'el jem.d: Remains of a second Roman amphitheater at Thysdrus, separate from the main amphitheater.
second amphitheatre d'el jem.a: Leveled remains of a second amphitheater at Thysdrus, older and much less well-preserved than the large amphitheater.
second amphitheatre d'el jem.c: A must-see alongside the large amphitheater, for those who are curious.

henchir-bir-el-menadla.d: An ancient archaeological site (Henchir) in the western part of the Mahdia Governorate, near the border with Kairouan.
henchir-bir-el-menadla.a: An ancient archaeological site (Henchir) in the western part of the Mahdia Governorate; modest remains.
henchir-bir-el-menadla.c: Mainly of archaeological interest: Check with local authorities for access information.

atelier de potier de sidi bouzid.d: An antique potter's workshop designated as a historic monument, near the city of Sidi Bouzid.
atelier de potier de sidi bouzid.a: An antique potter's workshop designated as a historic monument, near the city of Sidi Bouzid.
atelier de potier de sidi bouzid.c: Specialized website: Best approached with guidance to fully understand its value.

henchir bou zer.d: Ruins (henchir) in the northern part of the Sidi Bouzid Governorate.
henchir bou zer.a: Ancient ruins (henchir) in the northern part of the Sidi Bouzid Governorate; rather unspectacular remains.

camp de concentration de meheri-zebbeus.d: A former concentration camp established in 1939 in the Meknassy region.
camp de concentration de meheri-zebbeus.a: Site of a camp established in 1939 in the Meknassy region; a memorial site.
camp de concentration de meheri-zebbeus.c: A memorial site with no tourist facilities; please check with local sources for more information.

younga (iunca).d: An ancient Roman and Byzantine city south of Mahres, with Christian activity dating back to the 5th century.
younga (iunca).a: A Roman and Byzantine city south of Mahres, with a history of Christian activity dating back to the 5th century.
younga (iunca).c: A vast, largely undeveloped coastal area: be sure to bring water and sturdy shoes.

bordj el hassar (kerkennah).d: A historic fort in the Kerkennah Archipelago, near El Abbassia.
bordj el hassar (kerkennah).a: A medieval fortress with Hispano-Turkish influences on the Kerkennah Archipelago, near El Abbassia.
bordj el hassar (kerkennah).c: Combine this with an exploration of the archipelago and its traditional fishing practices.

rougga (bararus).d: The ancient Roman city of Bararus, located about 13 km southeast of El Jem.
rougga (bararus).a: The ancient Roman city of Bararus, located about ten kilometers southeast of El Jem.
rougga (bararus).c: A rural site with few amenities: guidance helps visitors locate and interpret it.

amphitheatre de bararus.d: Roman amphitheater at the ancient site of Bararus (Rougga), southeast of El Jem.
amphitheatre de bararus.a: Remains of a Roman amphitheater at the Bararus site (Rougga), southeast of El Jem.
amphitheatre de bararus.c: A must-see as part of the entire Rougga site, for lovers of antiquities.

kasr-erressass (acholla).d: A listed monument at the ancient site of Acholla.
kasr-erressass (acholla).a: A listed monument at the ancient site of Acholla, on the Sahel coast.
kasr-erressass (acholla).c: To be included in the tour of the Acholla site.

baptistere de sidi mansour.d: Ancient baptistery near Sidi Mansour, north of Sfax.
baptistere de sidi mansour.a: An ancient early Christian baptistery near Sidi Mansour, north of Sfax.
baptistere de sidi mansour.c: Discreet location: Check with locals for directions.

musee archeologique de sfax.d: Archaeological Museum of the City of Sfax.
musee archeologique de sfax.a: A city museum showcasing the region's ancient collections, including mosaics.
musee archeologique de sfax.c: A good introduction before exploring the medina and the ancient sites in the surrounding area.
musee archeologique de sfax.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening hours on site.

musee du patrimoine insulaire de kerkenn.d: Island Heritage Museum on the Kerkennah Archipelago.
musee du patrimoine insulaire de kerkenn.a: A museum dedicated to the heritage and traditions of the Kerkennah Archipelago, particularly fishing.
musee du patrimoine insulaire de kerkenn.c: A must-see to get a sense of island life before exploring the islands.
musee du patrimoine insulaire de kerkenn.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening hours on site.

eglise saint-pierre-et-saint-paul de sfa.a: A Catholic church from the colonial era, a testament to Sfax's diverse heritage.
eglise saint-pierre-et-saint-paul de sfa.c: Variable opening hours: Please check on site.

mosquee sidi amar kammoun.d: Historic mosque in the medina of Sfax.
mosquee sidi amar kammoun.a: Historic mosque in the medina of Sfax.
mosquee sidi amar kammoun.c: Place of worship: Observe from the outside and be discreet.

mosquee sidi elyes (sfax).d: Historic mosque in the medina of Sfax.
mosquee sidi elyes (sfax).a: Historic mosque in the medina of Sfax.
mosquee sidi elyes (sfax).c: Place of worship: Observe from the outside and be discreet.

mosquee sidi abdelmoula.d: Historic mosque in the medina of Sfax.
mosquee sidi abdelmoula.a: Historic mosque in the medina of Sfax.
mosquee sidi abdelmoula.c: Place of worship: Observe from the outside and be discreet.

mosquee el trouk (sfax).d: Historic mosque in the medina of Sfax.
mosquee el trouk (sfax).a: Ottoman mosque in the medina of Sfax, a remnant of the Turkish era.
mosquee el trouk (sfax).c: Place of worship: Observe from the outside and be discreet.

mosquee sidi ellakhmi.d: Historic mosque in the medina of Sfax.
mosquee sidi ellakhmi.a: Historic mosque in the medina of Sfax.
mosquee sidi ellakhmi.c: Place of worship: Observe from the outside and be discreet.

el abbassia (kerkennah).d: A town in the Kerkennah Archipelago, near the Bordj El Hassar Fort.
el abbassia (kerkennah).a: A town in the Kerkennah Archipelago, near the Bordj El Hassar Fort.
el abbassia (kerkennah).c: A convenient starting point for visiting the nearby fort.

phare de ras thyna.d: Lighthouse at Cape Ras Thyna, south of Sfax.
phare de ras thyna.a: The Cape Ras Thyna Lighthouse, south of Sfax, near the ancient site of Thaenae.
phare de ras thyna.c: Coastal landmark to be approached from the coast; to be used in conjunction with the Thyna site.

phare de l'ile charki (kerkennah).d: Charki Island Lighthouse (Kerkennah), at the entrance to the Sfax Channel.
phare de l'ile charki (kerkennah).a: Charki Island Lighthouse, at the entrance to the Sfax Channel, in the Kerkennah Archipelago.
phare de l'ile charki (kerkennah).c: You can see it during a boat tour around the archipelago.

camp de concentration de tniet-agareb.d: Former World War II concentration camp near Agareb.
camp de concentration de tniet-agareb.a: Site of a World War II camp near Agareb; a memorial site.
camp de concentration de tniet-agareb.c: A memorial site with no tourist facilities; please check with local sources for more information.

naraggara (sakiet sidi youssef).d: An ancient city in Africa Proconsularis, mentioned by Livy as being near Scipio’s camp before the Battle of Zama (202 B.C.). Corresponds to Sakiet Sidi Youssef, near the Algerian border.
naraggara (sakiet sidi youssef).a: The ruins of the ancient city mentioned by Livy near Scipio's camp before the Battle of Zama, in Sakiet Sidi Youssef.
naraggara (sakiet sidi youssef).c: Near the Algerian border: mainly of historical interest; be sure to check on access to the border area.

tajerouine.d: A town in the Kef Governorate, located about 38 km southwest of Kef, at the foot of Djebel Slata.
tajerouine.a: A stopover town at the foot of Djebel Slata, a starting point for exploring the surrounding sites.
tajerouine.c: More of a stopover than a destination: a good base for exploring the southwestern part of Kef.

dahmani (ebba ksour).d: A city in the Kef Governorate, formerly known as Ebba Ksour, located near the ancient site of Althiburos.
dahmani (ebba ksour).a: A town (formerly Ebba Ksour) that serves as the gateway to the nearby ancient site of Althiburos.
dahmani (ebba ksour).c: Make this your base for exploring nearby Althiburos.

le sers.d: A town located about 35 km southeast of El Kef, in a grain-growing region.
le sers.a: A town in a grain-growing region, with no major landmarks, located on the plain southeast of Kef.
le sers.c: Just a stop along the way; not particularly interesting from a tourist standpoint.

nebeur.d: A city in the Kef Governorate, near the Mellegue Dam.
nebeur.a: A village near the Mellegue Dam and its wadi landscapes.
nebeur.c: Combine this with a visit to the nearby Mellegue Dam.

touiref.d: A city in the northern part of the Kef Governorate.
touiref.a: A village in northern Kef, near the ruins of Masculula.
touiref.c: Possible starting point for a trip to the ancient site of Masculula.

jerissa.d: A city in the Kef Governorate, known for its iron mine and the Amazigh, Punic, and Roman ruins in the surrounding area.
jerissa.a: An iron-mining town surrounded by Amazigh, Punic, and Roman ruins.
jerissa.c: A must-see for anyone interested in mining heritage and the ruins scattered throughout the area.

kalaat es senam.d: A city in the western part of the Kef Governorate, at the foot of the Table de Jugurtha.
kalaat es senam.a: A town at the foot of the spectacular Table de Jugurtha, the starting point for the climb.
kalaat es senam.c: The perfect starting point before climbing the Table de Jugurtha: set out in the morning and bring water with you.

el ksour (le kef).d: A city and municipality in the Kef Governorate.
el ksour (le kef).a: A small town in the Kef Governorate, with no major landmarks.
el ksour (le kef).c: Just a quick stopover in the region.

masculula (henchir guergour).d: Ruins of ancient Masculula near Touiref, where Neo-Punic and Latin inscriptions were discovered (some of which are now in the Louvre).
masculula (henchir guergour).a: The ruins of ancient Masculula, where Neo-Punic and Latin inscriptions were found (some of which are now in the Louvre).
masculula (henchir guergour).c: A rural site near Touiref, largely undeveloped: recommended for epigraphy enthusiasts who have the coordinates.

siliana (ville).d: The capital of the Siliana Governorate, on the western edge of the Tunisian mountain range.
siliana (ville).a: The governorate capital, a starting point for exploring ancient sites and the mountains of the ridge.
siliana (ville).c: A good logistical base from which to explore Makthar, Ksar Lemsa, and Djebel Serj.

bou arada.d: A town in the northern part of the Siliana Governorate, at the foot of Djebel Bargou.
bou arada.a: A town at the foot of Djebel Bargou, near the ancient site of Apisa Maius.
bou arada.c: A hike toward Djebel Bargou and the ruins of Apisa Maius.

gaafour.d: A city in the Siliana Governorate, on the Northwest Railway Line.
gaafour.a: A stopover town on the Northwest Railroad line.
gaafour.c: Primarily a transportation hub; it has little tourist appeal in its own right.

bargou.d: A town nestled against the northern slope of Djebel Bargou (Siliana).
bargou.a: A village nestled against the northern slope of Djebel Bargou, in a lush mountainous setting.
bargou.c: Starting point for hikes on Djebel Bargou; pleasant in the spring.

rouhia.d: A town in the southern part of the Siliana Governorate, located in the highland grain-growing region.
rouhia.a: A town in the grain-growing highlands south of Siliana.
rouhia.c: A brief stop in a farming area.

el krib.d: A town in the northern part of the Siliana Governorate, near the ancient site of Musti.
el krib.a: A modern city adjacent to the ancient site of Musti, with its Arch of Gordian III and its macellum.
el krib.c: Park in El Krib and walk over to visit Musti, which is right next door.

thacia.d: A city from Roman Africa and a former bishopric, whose ruins are located near El Krib (Siliana).
thacia.a: The ruins of a Roman city and a former bishopric, near El Krib.
thacia.c: Combine this with the neighboring sites Musti and El Krib; a modest site worth checking out—be sure to note the coordinates.

apisa maius.d: An ancient city in Proconsular Africa and a bishopric (Tarf ech Chenah), near Bou Arada.
apisa maius.a: The ruins of a city in Proconsular Africa and a former episcopal see (Tarf ech Chenah).
apisa maius.c: Near Bou Arada; a secluded rural site, especially for archaeology enthusiasts.

kasserine (ville).d: The capital of the Kasserine Governorate, at the foot of Djebel Chambi, on the site of ancient Cillium.
kasserine (ville).a: The regional capital at the foot of Djebel Chambi, built on the site of ancient Cillium and serving as the gateway to the national park.
kasserine (ville).c: A base for exploring Djebel Chambi and the sites of Cillium and the Mausoleum of the Flavii.

feriana.d: A city in the southwestern part of the Kasserine Governorate, near the ancient site of Thelepte.
feriana.a: A town near the vast ancient site of Thelepte.
feriana.c: Make this your starting point for visiting Thelepte, which is about 5 km away.

foussana.d: A city in the northwestern part of the Kasserine Governorate, near the Algerian border.
foussana.a: A town in the northwest of Kasserine, between Djebel Bireno and the Algerian border.
foussana.c: Hike to Djebel Bireno; check access to this mountainous border area.

sbiba (ville).d: A city in the Kasserine Governorate located on the site of ancient Sufes (a basilica converted into a mosque).
sbiba (ville).a: The city stands on the site of ancient Sufes, whose basilica was converted into a mosque.
sbiba (ville).c: Look for the ruins of Sufes scattered throughout the city; a short tour.

thala (ville).d: A city in the Kasserine Governorate, at an elevation of about 1,017 m, one of the highest and coldest in Tunisia.
thala (ville).a: A high-altitude town (~1,017 m) that has retained its ancient name, one of the highest and coldest in Tunisia.
thala (ville).c: Dress warmly; combine this with a visit to the Thala archaeological site.

hassi el ferid.d: A city and the southwestern district of the Kasserine Governorate.
hassi el ferid.a: A small town in the southwestern part of Kasserine, with no major attractions.
hassi el ferid.c: Just a stop along the way.

el ayoun.d: A city and the northern district of the Kasserine Governorate.
el ayoun.a: A town in northern Kasserine with no notable landmarks.

jedelienne.d: A city and district in the northeastern part of the Kasserine Governorate.
jedelienne.a: A town in the northeastern part of Kasserine.

magel bel abbes.d: A city in the far southwest of the Kasserine Governorate, near the Algerian border.
magel bel abbes.a: A town in the far southwest of Kasserine, near the Algerian border.
magel bel abbes.c: Border area: Check for access information before you go.

musee archeologique de sbeitla.d: Museum in Sbeitla, across from the archaeological site, featuring mosaics and artifacts dating from prehistoric times to the Islamic period.
musee archeologique de sbeitla.a: Mosaics and artifacts dating from prehistoric times to the Islamic period, across from the Sufetula site.
musee archeologique de sbeitla.c: A short tour (~45 min) that can be combined with a visit to the archaeological site right across the street.
musee archeologique de sbeitla.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening hours on site.

bab souika.d: A historic gate and working-class neighborhood north of the medina of Tunis, the heart of traditional festive and cultural life.
bab souika.a: The lively square and its working-class neighborhood north of the medina, the traditional heart of Tunis’s festive life, near the Sidi Mahrez Mosque.
bab souika.c: More lively in the evenings and during the holiday season; a good starting point for a trip to Halfaouine.

bab menara.d: A gate in the Medina of Tunis on the southwest side, near Zitouna University.
bab menara.a: The gate on the southwest side of the medina, near Zitouna University, leading to an old residential neighborhood.
bab menara.c: A simple landmark marking the entrance to the Upper Medina; a quick visit.

bab bnet.d: A historic gate in the medina of Tunis, on the west side near the kasbah, connected to the administrative district.
bab bnet.a: The historic gate on the west side of the medina, near the kasbah and the former administrative district.
bab bnet.c: Don't miss this as you walk from Kasbah Square to the medina.

bab el fellah.d: The southern gate of the medina of Tunis, leading to the southern suburbs (cemeteries and zaouias).
bab el fellah.a: The southern gate of the medina, leading to the old southern suburbs (cemeteries and zaouias).
bab el fellah.c: A quick tour of the southern edge of the medina.

bab alioua.d: The southeastern gate of the Medina of Tunis, the historic starting point for routes to the Sahel and the south.
bab alioua.a: The southeast gate of the medina, the historic starting point for routes to the Sahel and the southern part of the country, is now located in a heavily trafficked area.
bab alioua.c: Busy intersection: just a landmark; no interior tour.

bab el allouj.d: A former gate in the walls of the Tunis medina, on the northwest side, near the kasbah.
bab el allouj.a: The old gate on the northwest side of the city wall, near the kasbah, a remnant of the medina's gate system.
bab el allouj.c: A quick stop to combine with the other gates in the Kasbah area.

palais saheb ettabaa.d: A beylical palace in the Halfaouine neighborhood, associated with the dignitary Saheb Ettabaa, early 19th century.
palais saheb ettabaa.a: The ornately decorated rooms and courtyard of the former beylical palace of the dignitary Saheb Ettabaa in the Halfaouine neighborhood.
palais saheb ettabaa.c: To be visited along with the Saheb Ettabaa Mosque and the bustling Halfaouine Square.

dar othman.d: Othman Dey Palace in the medina of Tunis, with a polychrome marble façade; one of the city's oldest palaces.
dar othman.a: The polychrome marble façade and ornate entrance of one of the oldest palaces in the medina, with its inner courtyard and garden.
dar othman.c: A little gem of residential architecture; a short visit to the heart of the medina.

dar el bey (palais du gouvernement).d: A former beylical palace in the Kasbah of Tunis, now the seat of the Prime Minister's Office.
dar el bey (palais du gouvernement).a: The imposing facade of the former Beylical Palace in the Kasbah, now the seat of the Presidency of the Government, on Kasbah Square.
dar el bey (palais du gouvernement).c: Official building not open to the public: best viewed from the square, along with the nearby Kasbah Mosque.

grande synagogue de tunis.d: The main synagogue in Tunis, built in the late 1930s in the modern part of the city in the Art Deco style.
grande synagogue de tunis.a: The Art Deco façade of the capital’s main synagogue, built in the modern part of the city in the late 1930s on Avenue de la Liberté.
grande synagogue de tunis.c: Restricted and secure access: Please check in advance if you plan to visit.

eglise saint-joseph de tunis.d: Catholic church in modern-day Tunis, built during the Protectorate era.
eglise saint-joseph de tunis.a: The Catholic building from the Protectorate era and its interior, in modern-day Tunis.
eglise saint-joseph de tunis.c: Worth seeing while strolling through the colonial downtown area.

eglise sainte-jeanne-d'arc de tunis.d: Catholic church in the northern district of Tunis (Lafayette), featuring colonial-era architecture.
eglise sainte-jeanne-d'arc de tunis.a: The colonial-era architecture of this church in the northern (Lafayette) neighborhood of the modern city.
eglise sainte-jeanne-d'arc de tunis.c: Of architectural interest above all; a brief stop in the modern city center.

musee national d'art moderne et contempo.d: Museum of Modern and Contemporary Tunisian Art, located in the City of Culture in Tunis.
musee national d'art moderne et contempo.a: The collections of modern and contemporary Tunisian paintings and sculptures, on display at the Cité de la Culture.
musee national d'art moderne et contempo.c: A contemporary addition to the Bardo; check the opening days of the Cité de la Culture.
musee national d'art moderne et contempo.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening hours on site.
