palais de ksar said.d: A 19th-century beylical palace near the Bardo, where the Treaty of the Bardo was signed (1881).
palais de ksar said.a: The 19th-century beylical palace, with its ornately decorated salons, and the historic setting where the 1881 Treaty of Bardo was signed, near the Bardo.
palais de ksar said.c: Combine this with a visit to the nearby Bardo Museum; check to see if it is open following its restoration.

musee paleochretien de carthage.d: A site museum showcasing the early Christian ruins of Carthage.
musee paleochretien de carthage.a: Early Christian artifacts and remains (sarcophagi, mosaics, architectural elements) on display at a site museum in the heart of Carthage.
musee paleochretien de carthage.c: A short themed stop to include in your tour of Carthage.
musee paleochretien de carthage.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening hours on site.

quartier hannibal (carthage).d: Remains of a Punic residential quarter on the southern slope of Byrsa, part of Carthage's urban layout prior to 146 B.C.
quartier hannibal (carthage).a: The streets and foundations of Punic dwellings unearthed on the southern slope of Byrsa, which bear witness to the urban layout of Carthage prior to 146 B.C.
quartier hannibal (carthage).c: Be sure to visit this site right after the Byrsa Museum to understand the original Punic city.

edifice a colonnes de carthage.d: Roman monument with colonnades in the archaeological site of Carthage, near the Roman villas.
edifice a colonnes de carthage.a: The Roman colonnaded monument in the archaeological area, near the villas on Odeon Hill.
edifice a colonnes de carthage.c: A modest ruin to be incorporated into the Roman Villas Trail.

synagogue beit mordekhai de la goulette.d: The La Goulette Synagogue, a testament to the Jewish community of the Port of Tunis.
synagogue beit mordekhai de la goulette.a: The synagogue in La Goulette, a testament to the port's former Jewish community and its cosmopolitan past.
synagogue beit mordekhai de la goulette.c: Access may be restricted; check it out during a walk through the La Goulette neighborhood.

kalaat el-andalous.d: A village founded by the Andalusians (Moriscos) in the 17th century, on a promontory overlooking the lower Medjerda River and Lake Ghar El Melh.
kalaat el-andalous.a: The Moorish village perched on its promontory, with its ancient alleyways and panoramic views of the lower Medjerda and the Ghar El Melh lagoon.
kalaat el-andalous.c: A beautiful view in the morning or evening light; best enjoyed in combination with the nearby mouth of the Medjerda River.

palais borj baccouche (ariana).d: Former Bey's residence in Ariana, featuring the vacation-style architecture typical of Tunisian dignitaries.
palais borj baccouche (ariana).a: The former Ariana Bey's summer residence and its architecture, typical of the vacation homes of Tunisian dignitaries.
palais borj baccouche (ariana).c: A modest site that is sometimes difficult to access; a quick stop for fans of Beylical heritage.

haras national de sidi thabet.d: Historic horse breeding farm in Sidi Thabet (Barb and Arab-Barb horses).
haras national de sidi thabet.a: The historic horse breeding farm dedicated to Barb and Arab-Barb horses, its stables, and its purebred horses.
haras national de sidi thabet.c: Of interest to horse lovers; check the visiting hours and conditions.

palais kobbet el nhas (manouba).d: A palatial pavilion with a copper dome in Manouba, a remnant of the beys’ summer residences.
palais kobbet el nhas (manouba).a: The palatial pavilion, crowned by its distinctive copper dome, is a remnant of the beys’ summer residences on the Manouba Plain.
palais kobbet el nhas (manouba).c: A small, secluded monument best viewed from the outside when passing through Manouba.

palais mourad bey (manouba).d: Former Beylical palace in Manouba, associated with the Mouradids, a resort area west of Tunis.
palais mourad bey (manouba).a: The ruins of the former beylical palace associated with the Muradids, a testament to the summer resorts west of Tunis.
palais mourad bey (manouba).c: A modest site; best viewed in conjunction with the other beylic residences in Manouba.

tebourba (thuburbo minus).d: A town in the Medjerda Valley, located on the site of the ancient Thuburbo Minus (a Roman colony), which was repopulated by Andalusians in the 17th century.
tebourba (thuburbo minus).a: The old Andalusian town in the Medjerda Valley and the remains of ancient Thuburbo Minus, including the ruins of the amphitheater.
tebourba (thuburbo minus).c: A stop on a countryside tour in the Medjerda Valley; combine this with a visit to the amphitheater and the Sidi Ali Azouz Mausoleum.

amphitheatre de tebourba.d: Remains of the Roman amphitheater of ancient Thuburbo Minus, in Tebourba.
amphitheatre de tebourba.a: The leveled remains of the Roman amphitheater of ancient Thuburbo Minus, nestled within the fabric of the modern city; a modest site.
amphitheatre de tebourba.c: A quick stop to include on a walk through Tebourba.

mausolee sidi ali azouz (tebourba).d: The zaouia and mausoleum of a Sufi saint in Tebourba, in the heart of the old city.
mausolee sidi ali azouz (tebourba).a: The zaouia and mausoleum of the Sufi saint, with its traditional decor, in the heart of Tebourba's old town.
mausolee sidi ali azouz (tebourba).c: Appropriate attire is required; a brief spiritual stop in the historic center.

pont-barrage d'el batan.d: An old water structure on the Medjerda River in El Batan, associated with the fulling mills in the valley.
pont-barrage d'el batan.a: The old waterworks on the Medjerda River and the remains of the fulling mills that made the valley famous for its textiles.
pont-barrage d'el batan.c: An interesting example of historic industrial heritage, worth seeing on a tour of the Medjerda Valley.

cimetiere militaire de massicault (borj.d: Commonwealth Military Cemetery (soldiers from the 1943 Tunisian Campaign).
cimetiere militaire de massicault (borj.a: The neat rows of headstones in the Commonwealth Cemetery, set in a well-maintained setting, where soldiers from the 1943 Tunisian campaign are buried.
cimetiere militaire de massicault (borj.c: A well-maintained place of contemplation; a simple visit, best combined with a trip to the Medjerda Valley.

palais de la mohammedia.d: The ruins of the beylical palace of Ahmed I Bey (mid-19th century) in La Mohammedia, nicknamed the “Tunisian Versailles,” remain unfinished.
palais de la mohammedia.a: The romantic ruins of Ahmed I Bey’s unfinished palace, nicknamed the “Tunisian Versailles,” whose arcades and sections of wall still stand on the plain.
palais de la mohammedia.c: A evocative, abandoned site; wear sturdy shoes and be careful among the ruins.

thermes d'oudhna (uthina).d: Large public baths in the Roman colony of Uthina (Oudhna), south of Tunis.
thermes d'oudhna (uthina).a: The large public baths of the Roman colony of Uthina, including their rooms and substructures, in the Oudhna archaeological site.
thermes d'oudhna (uthina).c: A must-see as part of the general tour of the Oudhna site.

cimetiere militaire allemand de borj ced.d: German military cemetery for World War II soldiers in Tunisia, on the hills above Borj Cedria.
cimetiere militaire allemand de borj ced.a: The German World War II military cemetery, with its massive crypt and graves clustered on the hills overlooking the gulf.
cimetiere militaire allemand de borj ced.c: A somber memorial site offering a view of the coast; a brief and understated visit.

aqueduc de zaghouan a carthage.d: A Roman aqueduct over 130 km long that carried water from the springs of Zaghouan to Carthage; long rows of arches are still visible. Coordinates of a section.
aqueduc de zaghouan a carthage.a: The long rows of Roman arches still standing on the plain, remnants of the more than 130 km of the aqueduct that carried water from Zaghouan to Carthage.
aqueduc de zaghouan a carthage.c: The arches are clearly visible from the Tunis–Zaghouan highway, especially toward Mohammedia/Oudhna; the light is beautiful as the sun dips low in the sky at the end of the day.

thermes romains de djebel oust.d: A Roman thermal bath complex built around a hot spring at Djebel Oust (mosaics), later converted into an early Christian complex.
thermes romains de djebel oust.a: The thermal spa complex centered around its hot spring, its original mosaics, and the early Christian structures that were built there afterward.
thermes romains de djebel oust.c: A little-visited specialty site; check for directions; best combined with a visit to Zaghouan.

grande mosquee de zaghouan.d: A Hanafi mosque in the city of Zaghouan, located in the historic district at the foot of the mountain.
grande mosquee de zaghouan.a: The Hanafi mosque and its minaret in the historic part of the city, at the foot of the djebel.
grande mosquee de zaghouan.c: Don't miss this during a stroll through the medina of Zaghouan and its fountains.

arc romain de zaghouan.d: Triumphal arch / Roman gate still standing in the city of Zaghouan, at the foot of the Temple of the Waters.
arc romain de zaghouan.a: The Roman arch (monumental gate) still standing in the city, at the foot of the path leading up to the Temple of the Waters.
arc romain de zaghouan.c: A stop along the way to the Temple of the Waters; a brief rest.

abthugni (henchir es-souar).d: A Roman city in the southern part of the Zaghouan Governorate, featuring a forum, a temple, and municipal ruins.
abthugni (henchir es-souar).a: The ruins of the forum, a temple, and municipal structures from the Roman city, scattered throughout the countryside in the southern part of the governorate.
abthugni (henchir es-souar).c: A modest, sparsely developed site for enthusiasts; a vehicle is required, and it is recommended to familiarize yourself with the area beforehand.

abbir maius.d: An ancient Roman city in the El Fahs region (Zaghouan), known for its inscriptions and ruins.
abbir maius.a: The scattered ruins of the ancient Roman city in the El Fahs region, known primarily for its inscriptions.
abbir maius.c: A site in a state of severe disrepair, best suited for enthusiasts of epigraphy and archaeology; be sure to hire a local guide.

segermes (henchir harat).d: Site of the ancient Roman city of Segermes, in the eastern part of the Zaghouan Governorate; Danish-Tunisian excavations.
segermes (henchir harat).a: The ruins of the ancient Roman city of Segermes, unearthed during Danish-Tunisian excavations east of the governorate.
segermes (henchir harat).c: A site of scientific interest with limited signage; check with local authorities before visiting.

eglise sainte-helene de zaghouan.d: A former Catholic church in the city of Zaghouan, a remnant of the Protectorate era.
eglise sainte-helene de zaghouan.a: The old Catholic church from the Protectorate period in the city of Zaghouan, a testament to colonial architecture.
eglise sainte-helene de zaghouan.c: A small historical landmark worth seeing while passing through Zaghouan.

arc de gordien iii (musti / el krib).d: A monumental arch from ancient Musti (El Krib), dated 239 according to an inscription, marking one of the city’s eastern entrances (a ceremonial gate rather than a triumphal arch). Approximate coordinates within the site.
arc de gordien iii (musti / el krib).a: A monumental arch dating from 239 marks one of the eastern entrances to ancient Musti.
arc de gordien iii (musti / el krib).c: Highlight of the Musti website; a quick tour as you browse the site.

marche romain (macellum) de musti / el k.d: Covered market (macellum) of ancient Musti, built of white limestone, located in the heart of the site alongside the forum, temples, and cisterns. Approximate coordinates within the site.
marche romain (macellum) de musti / el k.a: An ancient covered market made of white limestone, located at the heart of the site, which also features a forum, temples, and cisterns.
marche romain (macellum) de musti / el k.c: Check it out while browsing Musti; it only takes a few minutes to look at this specific item.

fort santiago (borj chikly).d: A fort stands on the islet of Chikly, in the middle of Lake Tunis. A former citadel of Roman origin, it was rebuilt by the Spanish governor of La Goulette between 1546 and 1550 (Santiago de Chikly). Designated a national cultural heritage site in 1993.
fort santiago (borj chikly).a: The Spanish-Ottoman fort standing on Chikly Islet in the middle of the lake, rebuilt in the 16th century on older foundations, within the bird sanctuary.
fort santiago (borj chikly).c: Access to the restricted area (permit, boat crossing): Please contact the INP before visiting.

citernes de bordj djedid (carthage).d: A large complex of Roman cisterns on the hill of Bordj Djedid in Carthage, near the shore, distinct from the cisterns at La Malga. Supplied by an arched aqueduct. Approximate coordinates.
citernes de bordj djedid (carthage).a: The extensive complex of vaulted Roman cisterns near the shore, distinct from those at La Malga, which helped supply water to Carthage.
citernes de bordj djedid (carthage).c: A discreet hydraulic component to be integrated into the Carthage circuit on the seaward side.

hotel sidi driss (decor star wars, ferme.d: A cave hotel in Matmata whose inner courtyard served as the setting for the interior of the Lars' farm (Luke Skywalker's home) in *Star Wars IV: A New Hope* (1977), and was reused for Episodes II (2002) and III (2005). Separate from downtown Matmata.
hotel sidi driss (decor star wars, ferme.a: A cave hotel in Matmata whose courtyard served as the interior of the Lars' farm in *Star Wars* (1977, then 2002 and 2005).
hotel sidi driss (decor star wars, ferme.c: This place is still in operation: you can stop by for a cup of tea or stay the night to take in the scenery; it gets crowded during peak hours.

ferme des lars / dome (chott el-djerid,.d: Exterior set of the Lars' farm (the dome/igloo) built on Chott el-Djerid, west of Nefta, for *Star Wars IV* (1977), and rebuilt for Episodes II and III. Distinct from Tozeur and Nefta.
ferme des lars / dome (chott el-djerid,.a: Exterior set of the Lars Farm (the dome) built on Chott el-Djerid, west of Nefta, for *Star Wars*.
ferme des lars / dome (chott el-djerid,.c: Access via the dirt road to the chott: A 4x4 is recommended, and come early in the morning to enjoy the light and the cool air.

bab el bhar (porte de france).d: A historic gate marking the boundary between the medina of Tunis and the European quarter, nicknamed the "Gate of France." The arch has stood alone since the demolition of the city walls.
bab el bhar (porte de france).a: the monumental arch marking the entrance to the medina of Tunis, the gateway between the Arab and European parts of the city.
bab el bhar (porte de france).c: A central landmark and the perfect starting point for a tour of the medina from Bourguiba Avenue.

parc national de l'ichkeul.d: A national park surrounding Lake Ichkeul and its wetlands, designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a Ramsar Site. A major stopover for migratory birds.
parc national de l'ichkeul.a: the lake and its wetlands; herds of buffalo; the eco-museum and the trail leading to the hot springs at the foot of the djebel; flocks of migratory birds.
parc national de l'ichkeul.c: Come in the winter to see waterfowl (coots, geese, flamingos); binoculars are recommended.

lac ichkeul.d: A brackish lake connected to the Bizerte Lagoon, in the heart of Ichkeul National Park. A Ramsar Site and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
lac ichkeul.a: National Park (UNESCO, Ramsar): hiking trails, an ecological museum, and, above all, the birdlife—flamingos, storks, pelicans, and thousands of coots and ducks overwintering here (229 animal species recorded). At the foot of the djebel (511 m), hot springs and traditional hammams, with Roman ruins nearby.
lac ichkeul.c: Come early in the morning or late in the afternoon (to avoid the heat); the best time to visit is from October to February for birdwatching. Access to the national park is regulated: check with the forestry administration (Eaux & Forêts / DGF).

parc national de djebel chambi.d: A national park home to Djebel Chambi, Tunisia's highest peak (1,544 m). A biosphere reserve covering an Aleppo pine forest.
parc national de djebel chambi.a: Tunisia's highest peak (1,544 m) is located in an Aleppo pine forest designated as a biosphere reserve, home to mountain wildlife.
parc national de djebel chambi.c: Restricted access: Check the requirements and safety guidelines, and plan for a full day and bring water for the hike.

parc national de bou hedma.d: A pre-Saharan steppe national park and biosphere reserve. A site for the reintroduction of antelopes and home to North Africa’s last acacia savanna.
parc national de bou hedma.a: A pre-Saharan steppe park and biosphere reserve, home to North Africa's last acacia savanna and reintroduced antelopes.
parc national de bou hedma.c: Restricted access: Please check with the park administration before visiting.

parc national de jbil.d: A Saharan national park located in the Grand Erg Oriental, the largest in Tunisia. A nature reserve home to gazelles and addax.
parc national de jbil.a: Tunisia's largest national park, located in the heart of the Grand Erg Oriental, is a refuge for gazelles and addax.
parc national de jbil.c: Deep Desert: Access by 4x4 vehicle with a licensed guide; water supplies are required.

parc national de boukornine.d: National park on Djebel Boukornine, a two-peaked mountain overlooking the Gulf of Tunis near Hammam Lif. Rich Mediterranean flora.
parc national de boukornine.a: The trails through the Mediterranean forest, the flora (cyclamen, irises), and the viewpoints overlooking the Gulf of Tunis from the Two-Horned Mountain.
parc national de boukornine.c: Perfect for springtime flower viewing; bring hiking shoes and water, and start from Hammam Lif.

parc national d'el feija.d: Kroumirie National Park, in a forest of cork oaks and zeen oaks. Habitat of the Barbary deer. Approximate coordinates.
parc national d'el feija.a: The Kroumirie forest of cork oaks and Zeen oaks, a refuge for the Barbary deer.
parc national d'el feija.c: Visit in the spring or fall to enjoy the forest and wildlife; bring a car and be prepared to walk, and watch the deer at dawn or dusk.

parc national de dghoumes.d: A national park on the edge of Chott el-Jerid, at the foot of the djebel. A reserve for pre-Saharan steppe and wildlife reintroduction.
parc national de dghoumes.a: A pre-Saharan steppe park on the edge of Chott el-Jerid, dedicated to the reintroduction of wildlife.
parc national de dghoumes.c: Wildlife viewing is best early in the morning; find out how to get there.

parc national de sidi toui.d: A desert steppe national park in southeastern Tunisia, near the Libyan border. A rehabilitation reserve for Saharan wildlife.
parc national de sidi toui.a: A desert steppe park in the southeast, dedicated to the rehabilitation of Saharan wildlife.
parc national de sidi toui.c: Remote area near the border: a guide and a 4x4 are recommended.

parc national de jebel orbata.d: A mountain national park in the Gafsa region, featuring gorges and springs. The flora represents a transition between the Mediterranean and Saharan zones.
parc national de jebel orbata.a: A mountain park near Gafsa, featuring gorges, springs, and flora that bridges the Mediterranean and Saharan ecosystems.
parc national de jebel orbata.c: Hiking in rugged terrain: wear good shoes, bring water, and set out early.

parc national de jebel serj.d: Tunisian Ridge National Park, which includes the Ain Soltane Cave and forests of Aleppo pine and holm oak.
parc national de jebel serj.a: The Ain Soltane Cave and the Aleppo pine and holm oak forests on the Tunisian mountain range.
parc national de jebel serj.c: A lovely spring outing in nature; be sure to bring good walking shoes and water.

parc national de jebel zaghouan.d: A national park protecting Djebel Zaghouan (1,295 m) and the Temple of the Waters, which supplied Carthage with water. A limestone massif along the ridge.
parc national de jebel zaghouan.a: The trails through the limestone massif, its views of the plain, and the Temple of the Waters nestled at its base.
parc national de jebel zaghouan.c: A cool hike at high altitude; be sure to wear good shoes and bring water. Best combined with a visit to the Temple of the Waters.

djebel zaghouan.d: A limestone peak rising to 1,295 m, one of the highest in northeastern Tunisia. It overlooks the Zaghouan Plain.
djebel zaghouan.a: The limestone peak overlooking the plain (1,295 m) and the sweeping views of northeastern Tunisia from its ridges.
djebel zaghouan.c: Hike for experienced hikers; set out early, bring water and a windbreaker; clear views on a sunny day.

ile de zembra.d: A mountainous island off the coast of Cap Bon, at the heart of the Zembra and Zembretta Islands National Park and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve.
ile de zembra.a: the island's cliffs and terrain; its marine life and bird colonies; the setting of the national park off the coast of Cap Bon.
ile de zembra.c: Protected reserve with restricted access: typically reached by boat tour.

parc national des iles de zembra et zemb.d: Marine and Island National Park off Cape Bon, a UNESCO biosphere reserve. An important seabird nesting site. Approximate coordinates.
parc national des iles de zembra et zemb.a: Marine and Island Park off the coast of Cap Bon, a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and an important seabird nesting site.
parc national des iles de zembra et zemb.c: Restricted access; consider a guided boat trip rather than a self-guided landing.

archipel de la galite.d: A volcanic archipelago off the northern coast of Tunisia, the country's northernmost point. A protected area and former monk seal habitat.
archipel de la galite.a: The volcanic archipelago off the northern coast of Tunisia, the country's northernmost point, a former habitat of the monk seal, and now a protected area.
archipel de la galite.c: Access is by boat only and weather permitting: plan on taking an organized tour during the summer months from Bizerte or Tabarka.

iles kerkennah.d: A low-lying, sandy archipelago off the coast of Sfax, surrounded by shoals and wetlands. Traditional fishing using the "charfia" method.
iles kerkennah.a: traditional Charfia fishing; the ports of Sidi Youssef and Sidi Frej; the low-lying beaches and palm groves; the Bordj El Hassar.
iles kerkennah.c: A slow-paced, timeless atmosphere; rent a bike and try the local grilled octopus.

ile de djerba.d: Tunisia's largest island, located in the Gulf of Gabès and connected to the mainland by an ancient causeway. A maritime oasis and lagoons.
ile de djerba.a: Tunisia's largest island, a maritime oasis with lagoons, connected to the mainland by an ancient causeway.
ile de djerba.c: Rent a bike or a car to explore the island; the beaches and villages are worth a visit.

iles kuriat.d: A small archipelago off the coast of Monastir, a nesting site for loggerhead sea turtles and a marine protected area.
iles kuriat.a: the white-sand beaches and crystal-clear waters; the old lighthouse; the loggerhead turtle nesting site.
iles kuriat.c: A day trip from Monastir during the season; be sure to bring a tent for shade and water—the island has no facilities.

ilot de chikly.d: A small islet in the middle of Lake Tunis, a nature reserve for birds and the site of a Spanish-Ottoman fort (Santiago).
ilot de chikly.a: The small bird sanctuary in the middle of the lake and the Spanish-Ottoman Fort Santiago that overlooks it.
ilot de chikly.c: Access is restricted to those with an INP permit, and a boat crossing is required: please arrange this in advance.

lac de tunis.d: A brackish lagoon between Tunis and the Gulf of Tunis, separated from the sea by a sandbar. A wetland that is home to flamingos and shorebirds.
lac de tunis.a: A lagoon on the outskirts of the capital: flamingos and shorebirds around Chikly Islet, home to the 16th-century Borj Chikly Fort. The La Goulette Road crosses the lake with a view of Tunis; on the Lac 1 side, there is a paved promenade and waterfront cafés.
lac de tunis.c: Winter birdwatching; binoculars are useful; beautiful morning light from the shore. Borj Chikly (islet) can only be visited occasionally, by boat.

lac de bizerte.d: A coastal lagoon connected to the Mediterranean Sea and Lake Ichkeul by channels. A body of water located in the northern part of the country.
lac de bizerte.a: A vast coastal lagoon connected to the Mediterranean Sea and Lake Ichkeul by channels. Along its shores lie the old port of Bizerte, its kasbah, and the canal—one of the most beautiful ports in the north.
lac de bizerte.c: Take a drive along it or admire it from the banks; combine this with a visit to the nearby Ichkeul Park and the old port of Bizerte.

oasis de tozeur.d: The Great Djerid Palm Grove on the shores of Chott el-Jerid, irrigated by a historic network of seguias. Coordinates centered on the town.
oasis de tozeur.a: The vast Djerid palm grove on the shores of Chott el-Jerid, irrigated by a historic network of seguias.
oasis de tozeur.c: A carriage ride or a walk through the palm grove, preferably in the morning.

oasis de nefta.d: The Djerid Palm Grove, known for the Corbeille de Nefta, a depression that serves as the source of the palm grove. Coordinates centered on the town.
oasis de nefta.a: The Djerid Palm Grove, renowned for the Corbeille de Nefta, a depression that serves as the oasis's water source.
oasis de nefta.c: The lookout point overlooking La Corbeille offers the best view; come at sunrise.
oasis de nefta.leg: Nefta is a holy city of Sufism, known as “Little Kairouan” for its hundreds of domes and marabouts; the saint Sidi Bou Ali is venerated there. Its Corbeille, a basin-shaped oasis, is considered a blessed place where springs once gushed forth.

oasis de montagne de chebika.d: A mountain oasis at the foot of Djebel el Negueb, fed by a spring and a waterfall. Coordinates centered on the village.
oasis de montagne de chebika.a: A mountain oasis at the foot of Djebel el Negueb, fed by a spring and a waterfall.
oasis de montagne de chebika.c: Trail to the waterfall: wear sturdy shoes and visit in the morning before it gets hot and the crowds arrive.

oasis de montagne de tamerza.d: Tunisia's largest mountain oasis, located in the Djerid Mountains, featuring gorges and waterfalls. An old village abandoned after the floods of 1969.
oasis de montagne de tamerza.a: Tunisia's largest mountain oasis, featuring gorges, waterfalls, and an old village abandoned after the floods of 1969.
oasis de montagne de tamerza.c: Be sure to wear good shoes for the gorges; the light and the weather are better in the morning.

oasis de montagne de mides.d: A mountain oasis perched on the edge of spectacular canyons, near the Algerian border. Coordinates centered on the village.
oasis de montagne de mides.a: An oasis perched on the edge of spectacular canyons, near the Algerian border.
oasis de montagne de mides.c: Approach the canyon's lookout points with caution; the low-angle light makes the landscape look even more stunning.

oasis de ksar ghilane.d: An isolated oasis on the edge of the Grand Erg Oriental, fed by a hot spring. The gateway to the Sahara Desert.
oasis de ksar ghilane.a: A secluded oasis on the edge of the Grand Erg Oriental, fed by a hot spring, at the gateway to the Sahara.
oasis de ksar ghilane.c: Access via dirt road: 4x4 recommended; swimming is possible at the spring, and you can enjoy sunsets over the dunes.

oasis maritime de gabes.d: A rare coastal oasis directly overlooking the sea in the Gulf of Gabès. A terraced palm grove threatened by urbanization and pollution. Coordinates centered on the city.
oasis maritime de gabes.a: A rare coastal oasis overlooking the sea, featuring a terraced palm grove that is now threatened by urbanization and pollution.
oasis maritime de gabes.c: A stroll under the palm trees during the cooler hours; the condition of the oasis varies by area.

chott el-jerid.d: The largest salt lake in the Tunisian Sahara, it dries up for much of the year and is covered with salt crusts. Mirages and colorful reflections.
chott el-jerid.a: The largest salt lake in the Tunisian Sahara dries up for much of the year, covered with salt crusts and mirages.
chott el-jerid.c: The road crosses the chott: stop at the designated spots at sunrise or sunset; the heat is overwhelming at noon.

chott el-gharsa.d: A salt depression located partly below sea level, northwest of Chott el-Jerid, near Tozeur.
chott el-gharsa.a: A salt depression, part of which lies below sea level, northwest of Chott el-Jerid near Tozeur.
chott el-gharsa.c: The reflections and colors are most beautiful in low-angle light; stay on the vehicle-accessible trails.

grand erg oriental.d: A vast sea of dunes in the Sahara stretching across Algeria and southwestern Tunisia (the Douz and Ksar Ghilane region). A location in Ksar Ghilane, the Tunisian gateway to the erg.
grand erg oriental.a: A vast sea of dunes in the Sahara stretching as far as southwestern Tunisia (Douz, Ksar Ghilane).
grand erg oriental.c: A 4x4, a guide, and water are essential; the dunes are breathtaking at sunrise and sunset.

dunes de douz.d: Known as the “Gateway to the Sahara,” Douz provides access to the vast dunes of the Grand Erg Oriental. Coordinates centered on the city.
dunes de douz.a: The Gateway to the Sahara: the great dunes of the Grand Erg Oriental, accessible from Douz.
dunes de douz.c: Meharee or 4x4 at sunrise/sunset for the most beautiful light; extreme heat during the day.

cap bon.d: A peninsula in northeastern Tunisia with a rugged coastline stretching from the Mediterranean Sea to the Gulf of Tunis. Coordinates at the northern tip of the cape.
cap bon.a: A peninsula with a rugged coastline between the Mediterranean Sea and the Gulf of Tunis, featuring a mix of rocky headlands, beaches, and villages; its northern tip is a well-known migration corridor for birds of prey.
cap bon.c: Ideal for a road trip (Korbous, El Haouaria, Kelibia); spring is a great time for watching migratory birds.

lagune de ghar el melh.d: A coastal lagoon and wetland at the foot of Djebel Nadhour, a Ramsar site renowned for its ramli gardens and birdlife. Coordinates centered on the village.
lagune de ghar el melh.a: The Ramsar lagoon and wetland at the foot of Djebel Nadhour, renowned for its traditional ramli gardens and birdlife.
lagune de ghar el melh.c: Beautiful light at the end of the day; birdwatching with binoculars and a tour of the town’s Ottoman forts to round out the day.

cote corallienne de tabarka.d: The rocky coastline of Kroumirie, known for its "Aiguilles" rock formations and coral reefs. Coordinates centered on the town.
cote corallienne de tabarka.a: the Aiguilles rocks; the Genoese fort; the coral reefs, a favorite spot for divers.
cote corallienne de tabarka.c: A renowned diving spot; the jazz festival brings the town to life in the summer.

cap negro (parc national jebel chitana-c.d: The Kroumirie Cape and Coastal National Park, combining coastal forest and sea cliffs in the northwestern part of the country.
cap negro (parc national jebel chitana-c.a: The cape and national park, which combine the Kroumirie coastal forest and sea cliffs in the northwestern part of the country.
cap negro (parc national jebel chitana-c.c: A wild and unspoiled area: Be sure to bring a suitable vehicle, water, and be prepared for a hike to reach the viewpoints.

ain draham (kroumirie).d: A mountain resort in the heart of the Kroumirie cork oak forests, one of the rainiest regions in Tunisia. Coordinates centered on the town.
ain draham (kroumirie).a: the cork oak forests; the houses with red-tiled roofs; the trails and viewpoints overlooking the forested mountains.
ain draham (kroumirie).c: The rainiest region in the country: lush and green in the spring, sometimes snowy in the winter—be sure to bring a jacket.

monts de matmata.d: A range of hills in southern Tunisia known as the Dahar, famous for its cave dwellings and arid landscapes. Coordinates centered on Matmata.
monts de matmata.a: The Dahar mountain range, known for its cave dwellings and arid landscapes.
monts de matmata.c: Scenic but winding roads: drive carefully and bring water.

sources thermales de korbous.d: A spa resort at Cap Bon, nestled in a coastal gorge and fed by hot springs, including the Ain Atrous, which flows into the sea. Coordinates centered on the town.
sources thermales de korbous.a: the spa town nestled in a coastal gorge; the Aïn Atrous hot spring, which flows into the sea.
sources thermales de korbous.c: Swimming is possible where the warm water meets the sea; scenic drive along the coast of Cap Bon.

hammam bourguiba.d: Hot spring in the Kroumirie forest area, near the Algerian border. Coordinates centered on the town.
hammam bourguiba.a: The hot spring nestled in the Kroumirie Forest, near the Algerian border.
hammam bourguiba.c: A relaxing stop after hikes in the forest; best combined with a visit to nearby Ain Draham.

djebel chambi (sommet).d: Tunisia's highest peak (1,544 m), located in the Tunisian Mountain Range near Kasserine. A forested massif of Aleppo pines, at the heart of a biosphere reserve.
djebel chambi (sommet).a: Tunisia's highest peak (1,544 m) and its mountain range covered with Aleppo pines, at the heart of a biosphere reserve.
djebel chambi (sommet).c: This hike must be done with a guide and a permit; check the access conditions and set out early with plenty of water.

djebel ghorra.d: The highest peak in the Kroumirie Mountains (1,250 m), on the Algerian-Tunisian border, in the wettest region of Tunisia. A nature reserve established in 2010.
djebel ghorra.a: The highest peak in the Kroumirie (1,250 m), Tunisia's wettest region and a nature reserve, on the Algerian-Tunisian border.
djebel ghorra.c: This hike is best enjoyed during the warmer months; be sure to bring sturdy shoes, water, and a warm jacket, as the summit can be foggy.

table de jugurtha.d: A spectacular mesa (1,271 m) near Kalaat es Senam (Le Kef), a historic refuge said to have been used by Jugurtha. Granaries and cave dwellings; UNESCO Tentative List.
table de jugurtha.a: A spectacular mesa (1,271 m) accessible via a staircase carved into the rock, featuring granaries, cave dwellings, and sweeping panoramic views (UNESCO tentative list).
table de jugurtha.c: Set out in the morning on a clear day; allow 2 to 3 hours for the round trip from Kalaat es Senam, and be sure to bring water and a hat.

djebel bireno.d: The second-highest peak in Tunisia (1,419 m), located between Foussana and Thala (Kasserine). A forest of Aleppo pines from which zgougou is harvested.
djebel bireno.a: Tunisia's second-highest peak (1,419 m) and its Aleppo pine forest, where zgougou is harvested.
djebel bireno.c: Hike in the mountains between Foussana and Thala; plan for a full day, bring water, and wear sturdy shoes.

djebel mghila.d: A mountain in the Dorsale Range between Kasserine and Sidi Bouzid (1,370 m), at the heart of a national park established in 2010.
djebel mghila.a: Montagne de la Dorsale (1,370 m) between Kasserine and Sidi Bouzid, at the heart of a national park established in 2010.
djebel mghila.c: Partially sensitive area: Check the access conditions before setting out on any hike.

djebel semmama.d: The Dorsale Mountain in the Kasserine Governorate (1,314 m), aligned with Djebel Chambi.
djebel semmama.a: A forested mountain in the Dorsale range (1,314 m), aligned with Djebel Chambi.
djebel semmama.c: Check for access information before going on any hike in this area.

djebel serj.d: A limestone mountain 1,357 m high, located about 20 km southeast of Siliana. Ain Dhab Cave; forests of Aleppo pine and holm oak.
djebel serj.a: A limestone mountain (1,357 m) featuring the Ain Dhab Cave and forests of Aleppo pine and holm oak.
djebel serj.c: About 20 km southeast of Siliana; a pleasant nature outing in the spring—be sure to bring water and hiking shoes.

djebel bargou.d: A mountain in the north-central region (1,266 m) southeast of Siliana, on the western branch of the Dorsale range. Source of the Miliane wadi.
djebel bargou.a: A mountain in the Dorsale Range (1,266 m), the source of the Miliane Wadi, set in lush green surroundings.
djebel bargou.c: A beautiful hiking area above Bargou; it's best to go in the spring, and be sure to bring water.

barrage de sidi salem.d: Tunisia's largest dam, completed in 1981 on the Medjerda River near Testour (~555 million m³, reservoir area of 4,300 ha).
barrage de sidi salem.a: The country's largest dam on the Medjerda River: a vast reservoir (~4,300 ha, ~555 million m³), with sweeping views of the water and freshwater fishing. Just a stone's throw from Testour and its Andalusian medina.
barrage de sidi salem.c: Beautiful panoramic view from the surrounding area; combine with a visit to Testour (mosque with an Andalusian minaret). An easy stopover from Béja or Medjez el-Bab.

barrage de beni m'tir.d: A dam built between 1946 and 1953 on the El Lil wadi southwest of Ain Draham, in the forested region of Kroumirie. Irrigation, drinking water, hydroelectric power.
barrage de beni m'tir.a: A dam built in the 1950s on the El Lil wadi, nestled in the Kroumirie cork oak forest, southwest of Aïn Draham—one of Tunisia’s greenest landscapes.
barrage de beni m'tir.c: A lovely spot with a panoramic view along the road to Aïn Draham; lush and green in the spring, sometimes misty and cool in the winter.

barrage de bou heurtma.d: Northwest Dam (Jendouba): The raising of the dam was completed in 2024, increasing its capacity to approximately 145 million m³.
barrage de bou heurtma.a: The Northwest Dam and its reservoir, in the Jendouba region.
barrage de bou heurtma.c: A nature stop along the region's roads; best combined with nearby ancient sites.

barrage mellegue.d: A 65-meter-high multi-arch dam on the Mellegue River, built from 1949 to 1956 (Le Kef). Irrigation, flood control, hydroelectric power.
barrage mellegue.a: A large, 65-meter-high multi-arch dam (1949–1956) on the Mellegue Wadi, set in a steep-walled wadi landscape.
barrage mellegue.c: Best enjoyed in combination with the nearby village of Nebeur; a pleasant view, with no tourist facilities.

barrage de sidi el barrak.d: Earth-fill dam (~265 million m³) completed around 2000 (Beja), near Tabarka. Ramsar Wetland.
barrage de sidi el barrak.a: A large earthen dam near Tabarka, adjacent to a Ramsar-designated wetland: a reservoir ideal for observing waterfowl, located in the wooded hinterland of Nefza.
barrage de sidi el barrak.c: Observe the birdlife around the reservoir; a nature stop along the road between Nefza and Tabarka. Check with locals before venturing off the trails.

barrage lakhmess.d: A 32-meter gravity dam was inaugurated in 1966 on the Lakhmess Wadi, about 15 km southeast of Siliana, at the foot of Jebel Serj.
barrage lakhmess.a: A 32-meter gravity dam (1966) on the Lakhmess Wadi, at the foot of Jebel Serj.
barrage lakhmess.c: A scenic stop about 15 km southeast of Siliana, best combined with a visit to Djebel Serj.

djebel ressas.d: An isolated limestone massif (~795 m) southeast of Tunis, a landmark in Greater Tunis. Former lead mines (the name means “lead mountain”). Approximate coordinates.
djebel ressas.a: The iconic limestone formation southeast of Tunis, its cliffs, its old lead mine tunnels, and the panoramic views from the heights.
djebel ressas.c: Hike for experienced hikers; early start, bring water and sturdy shoes; views of Greater Tunis from the summit.

sebkhet ariana.d: A brackish lagoon north of Tunis, separated from the sea by a sand dune barrier. A wetland home to flamingos and waterfowl.
sebkhet ariana.a: The brackish lagoon north of Tunis and its birdlife, particularly flamingos and waterfowl.
sebkhet ariana.c: Birdwatching from the surrounding area; good lighting at dawn; binoculars recommended.

sebkhet sejoumi.d: A vast salt flat southwest of Tunis, flooded in winter. An important wetland for birdlife, threatened by urbanization.
sebkhet sejoumi.a: The vast salt flat southwest of Tunis, which fills with water in the winter and is frequented by many waterbirds.
sebkhet sejoumi.c: Best seen in winter when it has water; observe from the surrounding area, avoiding run-down urban areas.

cap angela (ras ben sakka).d: The northern cape of Bizerte is considered the northernmost point of the African continent. Cliffs and rugged coastline.
cap angela (ras ben sakka).a: The cape, considered the northernmost point of the African continent, with its cliffs and rugged coastline.
cap angela (ras ben sakka).c: Visit for the symbolic significance of Africa's northernmost point and the panoramic views; the final stretch is a dirt road, so be sure to bring a suitable vehicle.

cap blanc (ras al-abiad).d: A white limestone promontory on the Bizerte coast, long considered the northernmost point of Africa, near Cape Angela.
cap blanc (ras al-abiad).a: The white limestone promontory overlooking the sea, near Cape Angela, which was long believed to be the northernmost point of Africa.
cap blanc (ras al-abiad).c: Combine this with a visit to nearby Cape Angela; beautiful light and views of the coast at the end of the day.

cap zebib.d: A rocky headland on the northeastern coast of Bizerte, extending into a series of small islets. An area of cliffs and fishing grounds.
cap zebib.a: The rocky headland on the northeastern coast of Bizerte, extended by small islets, in an area of cliffs and fishing grounds.
cap zebib.c: A peaceful coastal stretch; best enjoyed in combination with the other capes north of Bizerte.

cap serrat.d: The sand cape and cove of the Kroumirie Coast (Bizerte), nestled between forest and lagoon, are dominated by a lighthouse. A protected coastline.
cap serrat.a: The cape and its sandy cove, nestled between the forest and the lagoon and overlooked by a lighthouse, on the unspoiled coastline of Kroumirie.
cap serrat.c: An ideal secluded beach in the summer; the access road is long, so be sure to bring food and water, as there are few amenities.

iles cani.d: A small rocky archipelago off the northern coast of Bizerte, topped by a lighthouse. A nesting site for seabirds.
iles cani.a: The small rocky archipelago topped by a lighthouse, off the northern coast of Bizerte, a nesting site for seabirds.
iles cani.c: Accessible only by boat and weather permitting; best enjoyed as part of an organized boat trip.

djebel ichkeul.d: An isolated limestone mountain overlooking Lake Ichkeul, in the national park. Mediterranean flora and fauna, with hot springs at its base.
djebel ichkeul.a: The isolated limestone mountain overlooking the lake, with its Mediterranean flora and fauna and the hot springs at its base.
djebel ichkeul.c: Hike up the park's trails to enjoy the view of the lake; binoculars are helpful, and the best time to visit is from fall through spring.

embouchure de la medjerda.d: Delta and mouth of the Medjerda, Tunisia's main river, on the northern coast near Kalaat el-Andalous. Alluvial plain and coastal wetland.
embouchure de la medjerda.a: The delta of Tunisia's main river, its floodplain, and the coastal wetland teeming with birds, near Kalaat el-Andalous.
embouchure de la medjerda.c: Combine this with a visit to the hilltop village of Kalaat el-Andalous; a great spot for birdwatching.

sebkha de kelbia.d: An intermittent saltwater lake (~8,000 ha) in the Kairouan Plain, north of the city. The second-largest wetland after Ichkeul, it has been a nature reserve since 1993. Approximate coordinates.
sebkha de kelbia.a: An intermittent salt lake (~8,000 ha) north of Kairouan, a nature reserve and a major wetland for waterbirds after Ichkeul.
sebkha de kelbia.c: Of interest to birdwatchers, especially after it rains, when the lake is full; binoculars are recommended.

sebkhet halk el menzel.d: Coastal salt lagoon in the Sousse Governorate, near Sidi Khelifa. Ramsar wetland (~1,450 ha), important for birdlife. Approximate coordinates.
sebkhet halk el menzel.a: Coastal salt lagoon (~1,450 ha) near Sidi Khelifa, a Ramsar wetland of international importance for birdlife.
sebkhet halk el menzel.c: An undeveloped natural site; best visited for quiet birdwatching.

ile zembretta.d: A small islet in the Gulf of Tunis, about 8 km east of Zembra (about 2 ha). Together with Zembra, it forms an important area for seabird conservation.
ile zembretta.a: A small islet (~2 ha) east of Zembra, which together with Zembra forms a key area for seabird conservation.
ile zembretta.c: A protected islet with restricted access; viewing is permitted only from the sea.

foret de dar chichou.d: Cap Bon State Forest (>6,000 ha) north of El Haouaria (Nabeul). A Mediterranean dune forest resulting from dune stabilization efforts that began around 1930.
foret de dar chichou.a: A state-owned dune forest covering more than 6,000 ha north of El Haouaria, formed as a result of the stabilization of the Cap Bon dunes, which began around 1930.
foret de dar chichou.c: A pleasant setting for a nature break between the capes; stay on the trails.

djebel orbata (sommet).d: A limestone mountain (1,165 m) east of Gafsa, extending about 60 km to the northeast. The area is protected by the national park. Approximate coordinates.
djebel orbata (sommet).a: A limestone mountain rising to 1,165 m east of Gafsa, protected by the national park.
djebel orbata (sommet).c: This hike is for walkers only: early start, bring water and sturdy shoes.

gorges de selja.d: A several-kilometer-long, steep-sided valley through which the Selja wadi flows, between Metlaoui and Redeyef (Gafsa). Designated a nature reserve (675 ha) in 2009, it is home to the red lizard.
gorges de selja.a: The steep-walled valley of the Selja Wadi between Metlaoui and Redeyef, a nature reserve through which the Red Lizard passes.
gorges de selja.c: The train is the best way to explore the gorges; be sure to book in high season.

oasis de gafsa.d: Historic oasis system (~700 ha) on the northern edge of the Sahara (Sakdoud, Ksar, Lela, Gafsa, El Guettar), featuring a three-tiered cultivation system. Designated a GIAHS in 2011.
oasis de gafsa.a: A historic oasis system with a three-tiered cultivation system, recognized as a Global Important Agricultural Heritage System (GIAHS, 2011).
oasis de gafsa.c: A walk through the palm grove during the cooler hours of the day; a guide explains the irrigation system.

sebkhet en noual.d: A vast, salt-covered depression in the central steppe (~17,000 ha), on the border between Sidi Bouzid and Sfax. A Ramsar Wetland since 2007.
sebkhet en noual.a: A vast, salt-covered depression in the central steppe (~17,000 ha), a Ramsar wetland on the border between Sidi Bouzid and Sfax, frequented by waterbirds.
sebkhet en noual.c: Ornithological interest: Bring binoculars, and avoid walking on the salt crusts.

marais salants de thyna (sfax).d: Salt flats and coastal wetland south of Sfax, along the Gulf of Gabès near Thyna. Large protected wetland, designated a Ramsar Site in 2007, important for waterbirds. Approximate coordinates.
marais salants de thyna (sfax).a: Salt flats and coastal wetlands south of Sfax (Ramsar), important for flamingos and waterbirds.
marais salants de thyna (sfax).c: Bring binoculars; watch from the levees without disturbing the birds.

corbeille de nefta.d: A natural basin-shaped depression beneath the Nefta hills, fed by springs that irrigate the original oasis. An iconic site in the Djerid region.
corbeille de nefta.a: A natural basin-shaped depression beneath the Nefta Hills, fed by springs that irrigate the original oasis.
corbeille de nefta.c: The lookout offers the best view; come at sunrise to catch the light.

palmeraie de douz.d: A vast palm grove (>500,000 palm trees) surrounding Douz, the gateway to the Sahara (Kebili). Coordinates centered on the city.
palmeraie de douz.a: A vast palm grove with more than 500,000 palm trees surrounding Douz, the gateway to the Sahara.
palmeraie de douz.c: A shaded stroll through the palm grove; combine it with an excursion to the nearby dunes.

chott el-fejaj.d: A long, muddy, endorheic lake arm extending eastward from Chott el-Jerid, north of Nefzaoua. It dries up for much of the year.
chott el-fejaj.a: A long, muddy, endorheic lake arm extending eastward from Chott el-Jerid; it dries up for much of the year.
chott el-fejaj.c: Unprepared, icy terrain: Stay on the safe trails and avoid the crust that forms after rain.

djebel dahar.d: A mountain range in the southeast (~713 m, ~6,500 km²), in the Tataouine and Medenine regions. An arid plateau dotted with hilltop Berber villages and ksour.
djebel dahar.a: The arid plateau of the southeast, dotted with hilltop Berber villages and ksour, near Tataouine and Medenine.
djebel dahar.c: An ideal region for a tour of the ksour; a 4x4 or guide is recommended for the trails.

djebel tebaga.d: A mountain range north of Chott el-Jerid near Kebili, featuring fossil reefs from the marine Permian period. Site of the Tebaga Breakthrough (Battle of the Mareth Line, 1943).
djebel tebaga.a: A mountain range north of Chott el-Jerid featuring Permian fossil reefs, site of the Tebaga breakthrough (1943).
djebel tebaga.c: Geological and historical interest; the terrain is arid, so be sure to bring water and a hat.

el hamma du jerid.d: An oasis town in the Tozeur Governorate, on the northern edge of the Djerid, known for its hot springs. A palm grove irrigated by thermal springs.
el hamma du jerid.a: An oasis town on the northern edge of the Djerid, irrigated by hot springs.
el hamma du jerid.c: Very hot springs: Find out which pools are open to visitors.

lagune de korba (sebkha korba).d: A coastal lagoon north of Korba, an important wetland for migratory birds in Cap Bon.
lagune de korba (sebkha korba).a: A coastal lagoon north of Korba, a wetland of importance for migratory birds in the Cap Bon region.
lagune de korba (sebkha korba).c: Bird-watching site; migration seasons are the best times to visit; binoculars are recommended.

sebkhet soliman.d: Sebkha de Soliman, a wetland in Cap Bon and a Ramsar site of importance for waterbirds.
sebkhet soliman.a: The Cap Bon Wetland, a Ramsar Site, is important for waterbirds.
sebkhet soliman.c: The focus is primarily on birdwatching; observe from a distance so as not to disturb the birds.

sebkha el maamourah.d: Sebkha El Maâmourah, a coastal wetland southeast of Cap Bon.
sebkha el maamourah.a: Coastal wetland southeast of Cap Bon.
sebkha el maamourah.c: A modest natural site, especially for observing waterfowl.

sebkha tazerka.d: Sebkha Tazerka, a wetland on the east coast of Cap Bon.
sebkha tazerka.a: Wetland on the east coast of Cap Bon.
sebkha tazerka.c: A quiet birding spot; few amenities on site.

grotte des chauves-souris (el haouaria).d: Bat Cave near El Haouaria, at the tip of Cape Bon.
grotte des chauves-souris (el haouaria).a: A cave inhabited by bats, near El Haouaria at the tip of Cape Bon.
grotte des chauves-souris (el haouaria).c: Best enjoyed in combination with the nearby Roman quarries; a flashlight and appropriate footwear are recommended.

djebel hammamet.d: A coastal mountain range southwest of Hammamet.
djebel hammamet.a: A coastal mountain range southwest of Hammamet overlooking the bay.
djebel hammamet.c: A scenic route for a short hike; set out early on hot days.

djebel el haouaria.d: Topography of the northern tip of Cape Bon, an important migration corridor for birds of prey. Approximate coordinates.
djebel el haouaria.a: Topography of the northern tip of Cape Bon, an important migration corridor for birds of prey.
djebel el haouaria.c: Spring is the best season for watching birds of prey migrate; binoculars are a must.

sebkha de sidi el hani (sousse).d: A large salt lake (~36,000 ha) southwest of Sousse. A salt flat subject to periodic flooding.
sebkha de sidi el hani (sousse).a: A large salt lake (~36,000 ha) southwest of Sousse; a salt flat subject to periodic flooding.
sebkha de sidi el hani (sousse).c: A salt landscape that changes with the seasons; an undeveloped natural site.

sebkha de moknine.d: Salt depression southeast of Moknine, a wetland of importance for birdlife.
sebkha de moknine.a: Salt depression southeast of Moknine, a wetland of importance for birdlife.
sebkha de moknine.c: Of interest to birdwatchers; best combined with a visit to Moknine.

marais salants de monastir.d: A wetland (~1,000 ha) designated as a Ramsar site in 2012, important for pink flamingos.
marais salants de monastir.a: A wetland covering approximately 1,000 ha, designated as a Ramsar Site in 2012, and important for pink flamingos.
marais salants de monastir.c: A great spot for watching flamingos; come early in the morning with binoculars.

ile conigliera.d: A small island off the coast of the Gulf of Monastir, part of the Kuriat Archipelago.
ile conigliera.a: A small island off the coast of the Gulf of Monastir, part of the Kuriat Archipelago.
ile conigliera.c: It can only be reached by sea, as part of an excursion to the Kuriat Islands.

chott oulad amar.d: Salt flat (chott) in the Bekalta region, near Ras Dimass.
chott oulad amar.a: Salt flat (chott) in the Bekalta region, near Ras Dimass.
chott oulad amar.c: An undeveloped natural site; worth visiting, perhaps, along with the nearby ruins of Thapsus.

bahiret el bibane.d: Large southeastern coastal lagoon (Medenine), designated a Ramsar Site in 2007, important for fishing and birdlife.
bahiret el bibane.a: A large coastal lagoon in the southeast, a significant Ramsar site for fishing and birdlife.
bahiret el bibane.c: Binoculars are useful for birdwatching; the light is best early in the morning.

sebkhet el melah de zarzis.d: A vast salt flat near Zarzis (~150 km²), separated from the sea by a dune ridge, where salt is harvested.
sebkhet el melah de zarzis.a: A vast salt flat (~150 km²) near Zarzis, separated from the sea by a dune ridge and used for salt production.
sebkhet el melah de zarzis.c: Photogenic reflections in low-angle light; stay on the accessible paths.

golfe de gabes (petite syrte).d: A large gulf on the southeastern coast opening onto the Mediterranean Sea, formerly known as Petite Syrte, with a significant tidal range.
golfe de gabes (petite syrte).a: A large gulf on the southeastern coast, the ancient Petite Syrte, notable for its significant tidal range.
golfe de gabes (petite syrte).c: The tidal range exposes a large portion of the foreshore: check the tide tables for the beach.

oued akarit.d: A coastal waterway north of Gabès that flows into the gulf; a site of prehistoric significance.
oued akarit.a: A coastal river north of Gabès, notable for its prehistory and as the site of a battle in 1943.
oued akarit.c: Site with no tourist facilities: primarily of historical and natural interest.

djebel bouramli.d: A mountain in the southwest (Gafsa), extending from Djebel Orbata and bordering the Gafsa Plain.
djebel bouramli.a: A mountain in the southwest that extends from Djebel Orbata and borders the Gafsa Plain.
djebel bouramli.c: Arid terrain: recommended for well-equipped hikers, with water and an early start.

ain kriz.d: A natural spring north of Tozeur, in the El Oudiane oasis group (Jerid).
ain kriz.a: A natural spring north of Tozeur, in the El Oudiane oasis group (Jerid).
ain kriz.c: Take a refreshing break in the palm grove; please respect the layout of the spring.

phare du cap angela.d: Lighthouse marking Cape Angela (Ras ben Sakka), the northernmost point of continental Africa.
phare du cap angela.a: The lighthouse marking Cape Angela (Ras ben Sakka), the northernmost point of mainland Africa.
phare du cap angela.c: A landmark at the tip of the continent; combine this visit with Cape Angela and Cape Blanc.

cap sidi ali el mekki.d: A rocky cape (formerly Cape Farina) enclosing Ghar el Melh Bay, a popular beach and an Ottoman fort.
cap sidi ali el mekki.a: The rocky headland that closes off Ghar el Melh Bay, with its popular beach and Ottoman fort—formerly known as Cap Farina.
cap sidi ali el mekki.c: A beautiful beach that gets very crowded in the summer: come early, and combine this visit with a trip to Raf Raf and the Ghar el Melh lagoon.

ile de la galite (ile principale).d: The largest island in the volcanic La Galite archipelago, a nature reserve rich in birdlife and flora.
ile de la galite (ile principale).a: The largest island in the volcanic La Galite archipelago, a nature reserve rich in birdlife and flora.
ile de la galite (ile principale).c: Access by boat is available only during the summer months; plan an organized tour and check the weather forecast.

le galiton.d: A rocky islet in the La Galite archipelago with a lighthouse, the westernmost point of Tunisia.
le galiton.a: The rocky islet with a lighthouse, Tunisia's westernmost point, in the La Galite archipelago.
le galiton.c: A remote offshore site: worth seeing on a boat trip around La Galite.

ile pilau.d: A small island off the coast of Raf Raf and Cape Sidi Ali el-Mekki.
ile pilau.a: The small island off the coast of Raf Raf and Cape Sidi Ali el-Mekki, with its distinctive silhouette facing the beach.
ile pilau.c: Best viewed from Raf Raf Beach; there are no visitor facilities on the island.

ile plane.d: A low-lying island off Cape Sidi Ali el-Mekki, topped by a lighthouse.
ile plane.a: The low-lying island topped by a lighthouse, off the coast of Cape Sidi Ali el-Mekki.
ile plane.c: Visible from the coast; a must-see when exploring Ghar el Melh Bay.

iles fratelli.d: A small rocky archipelago off the northwest coast, between Cape Serrat and Cape Negro.
iles fratelli.a: The small rocky archipelago off the northwest coast, between Cape Serrat and Cape Negro.
iles fratelli.c: A navigational marker visible from the Kroumirie coastline; no shore visit.

garaa sejnane.d: A wetland (marsh) in the northwest near Sejnane, important for migratory birds.
garaa sejnane.a: The wetland and marsh near Sejnane, which is important for migratory birds.
garaa sejnane.c: Visit during the wet season to see waterfowl; binoculars are recommended, and this trip can be combined with a visit to the town of Sejnane.

barrage de joumine.d: A reservoir feeding Lake Ichkeul, in the southwestern part of the governorate.
barrage de joumine.a: The reservoir that feeds Lake Ichkeul, in the southwestern part of the Bizerte Governorate.
barrage de joumine.c: A natural landmark related to the Ichkeul water system; worth seeing on your way to the park.

barrage de sejnane.d: Dam and reservoir on the Sejnane Wadi, in the northwestern part of the governorate.
barrage de sejnane.a: The dam and its reservoir on the Sejnane Wadi, in the northwestern part of the governorate.
barrage de sejnane.c: Panoramic overlook on the road to Sejnane; best enjoyed in conjunction with the nearby wetlands.

barrage de kasseb.d: A dam west of Beja, supplying drinking water to Greater Tunis, at the foot of the Kroumirie.
barrage de kasseb.a: The dam west of Béja, which supplies Greater Tunis with drinking water, at the foot of the Kroumirie.
barrage de kasseb.c: A lush spring retreat; a stop along the forest roads of the Béja region.

djebel khroufa.d: Mountain and nature reserve in the Nefza region, in the northwestern forest range.
djebel khroufa.a: The mountain and nature reserve in the Nefza region, a forested massif in the northwest.
djebel khroufa.c: A pleasant hike through the forest in the spring and fall; be sure to bring water and sturdy shoes.

aiguilles de tabarka.d: A remarkable rock formation on the Tabarka coast: sandstone spires rising from the seashore.
aiguilles de tabarka.a: The sandstone spires rising from the seashore, an iconic rock formation along the Tabarka coast.
aiguilles de tabarka.c: A great spot for sunset photos; combine it with a visit to the Genoese Fort and the Coral Coast.

parc national de oued zen.d: Kroumirie National Park, which protects the oak-zenes forest and the Barbary deer, south of Tabarka.
parc national de oued zen.a: The Kroumirie oak forest and the Barbary deer it shelters, south of Tabarka.
parc national de oued zen.c: Plan your visit for spring or fall; make sure to bring a car and be prepared to walk to get into the forest.

tourbieres de dar fatma.d: High-altitude peatland nature reserve in Kroumirie, a rare wetland in Tunisia. Approximate coordinates.
tourbieres de dar fatma.a: The high-altitude peat bogs of Kroumirie, a rare wetland in Tunisia, located within a nature reserve.
tourbieres de dar fatma.c: A sensitive, largely undeveloped natural area: walk with caution—ideally with a guide—in the spring.

reserve naturelle d'ain zana.d: Kroumirie Nature Reserve near Ghardimaou: oak forests and forest biodiversity.
reserve naturelle d'ain zana.a: The oak forest and forest biodiversity of Kroumirie, near Ghardimaou.
reserve naturelle d'ain zana.c: A nature stop worth combining with a visit to Ghardimaou and El Feija Park; best in the spring.

barrage barbara.d: Dam and reservoir in Kroumirie, on the Oued el Kebir.
barrage barbara.a: The dam and its reservoir in Kroumirie, on the Oued el Kebir, set amid wooded surroundings.
barrage barbara.c: A scenic stop along the forest roads of the northwest; a lush, green setting during the rainy season.

djebel ousselat.d: A limestone mountain in the Tunisian Ridge, the highest point in the Kairouan Governorate (Oueslatia).
djebel ousselat.a: A limestone mountain in the ridge, the highest point in the Kairouan Governorate, in the Oueslatia region.
djebel ousselat.c: Mid-mountain hike: Make sure you're wearing the right shoes and have plenty of water.

djebel trozza.d: Mountain range in the Kairouan Governorate, near Haffouz.
djebel trozza.a: Mountain range in the Kairouan Governorate, near Haffouz.
djebel trozza.c: A natural setting with few amenities: be sure to bring water and sturdy shoes.

sebkha tsaacha.d: Sebkha (salt flat) in the southern part of the Kairouan Governorate.
sebkha tsaacha.a: Salt flat (sebkha) in the southern part of the Kairouan Governorate.
sebkha tsaacha.c: This is a wetland—please observe it from a distance; avoid venturing onto the salt crust.

ras djezira (chebba).d: A coastal cape in the southern part of the governorate, near Chebba.
ras djezira (chebba).a: A coastal cape in the southern part of the Mahdia Governorate, near Chebba.
ras djezira (chebba).c: A pleasant view of the sea; wear sturdy shoes on the rocks.

ras salakta.a: Salakta Headland, near the ancient site of the same name.
ras salakta.c: Combine this with a visit to the Salakta site and museum.

sebkha el ghorra.d: Sebkha (a temporary salt lake) west of the Mahdia Governorate.
sebkha el ghorra.a: A temporary salt lake (sebkha) west of the Mahdia Governorate.
sebkha el ghorra.c: A wetland best viewed from a distance, especially during the wet season.

sebkha cherita.d: Sebkha in the western part of the Mahdia Governorate.
sebkha cherita.a: Sebkha in the western part of the Mahdia Governorate.
sebkha cherita.c: Nature-watching highlight: Watch waterfowl without venturing onto the salt flats.

sebkha ben ghiadha.c: A wetland best viewed from the surrounding area; binoculars are recommended.

reserve naturelle djebel rihana-djebel g.d: Nature reserve (~2,000 ha) covering the Rihana and Goulebe mountains, Souk Jedid district.
reserve naturelle djebel rihana-djebel g.a: A nature reserve covering approximately 2,000 ha, encompassing the Rihana and Goulebe mountains, in the Souk Jedid district.
reserve naturelle djebel rihana-djebel g.c: Reservation access: Check the terms and conditions before you go.

plaine de gammouda.d: The Gammouda Agricultural Plain, in the central part of the Sidi Bouzid Governorate.
plaine de gammouda.a: Agricultural plain in the central part of the Sidi Bouzid Governorate.
plaine de gammouda.c: Rural scenery rather than a tourist attraction: something to pass through as you drive along the road.

djebel chlel.d: A mountain in the eastern part of the Sidi Bouzid Governorate, near Ouled Haffouz.
djebel chlel.a: A mountain in the eastern part of the Sidi Bouzid Governorate, near Ouled Haffouz.
djebel chlel.c: A natural setting with few amenities: be sure to bring water and sturdy shoes.

iles kneiss.d: An archipelago and nature reserve (Ramsar) in the Gulf of Gabès, important for migratory birds.
iles kneiss.a: The Gulf of Gabès Archipelago and Ramsar Nature Reserve, which are important for migratory birds.
iles kneiss.c: Protected Area: Access by sea; arrangements must be made locally and with due regard for birdlife.

reserve naturelle d'el gonna.d: Nature reserve and protected area in the Sfax Governorate.
reserve naturelle d'el gonna.a: Nature Reserve and Protected Area in the Sfax Governorate.
reserve naturelle d'el gonna.c: Reservation access: Check the terms and conditions before you go.

plage de chaffar.d: A beach on the Gulf of Gabès coast, south of Sfax.
plage de chaffar.a: Beach on the Gulf of Gabès, south of Sfax.
plage de chaffar.c: A place for swimming and relaxation; check the conditions on site.

sebkha el jem.d: Sebkha (salt flat) in the northern part of the Sfax Governorate, near El Jem.
sebkha el jem.a: Sebkha (salt flat) in the northern part of the Sfax Governorate, near El Jem.
sebkha el jem.c: A wetland best viewed from a distance, especially during the wet season.

zones humides de la skhira.d: Wetland complex in the southern part of the Sfax Governorate (Chott el Guetayate, Akarit/Rekhama/Meleh wadis), important for birdlife.
zones humides de la skhira.a: Wetland complex in southern Sfax Governorate (Chott el Guetayate, Akarit, Rekhama, and Meleh wadis), important for birdlife.
zones humides de la skhira.c: Ornithological interest: binoculars are useful for observing birds from a distance.

djebel dyr (dyr el kef).d: A table mountain in the Tunisian Atlas Mountains (approx. 1,074 m) overlooking the city of El Kef, which is built on its cliff.
djebel dyr (dyr el kef).a: A table mountain (approx. 1,074 m) overlooking the city of El Kef, which is built on its cliff, offering sweeping panoramic views.
djebel dyr (dyr el kef).c: Head up to the lookout point overlooking Le Kef and the plain, preferably in the late afternoon.

barrage de siliana.d: Dam on the Siliana Wadi, for irrigation and water supply.
barrage de siliana.a: A dam on the Siliana River, set against a backdrop of plains and hills.
barrage de siliana.c: A simple scenic stop near Siliana.

parc national de chambi.d: A national park established in 1980 around Djebel Chambi, a UNESCO biosphere reserve.
parc national de chambi.a: The national park was established in 1980 around Djebel Chambi, a UNESCO biosphere reserve and the country's highest peak.
parc national de chambi.c: Restricted access: Check the access requirements and security measures before your visit, and plan for a full day.

parc du belvedere.d: The largest and oldest urban park in Tunis (1892), located on a wooded hill overlooking the city and the lake.
parc du belvedere.a: Tunis's largest park, set on a wooded hill; the Ottoman koubba; the panoramic view of the city and the lake.
parc du belvedere.c: A pleasant morning stroll in the shade of olive and pine trees, in the heart of Tunis.

cap carthage.d: A rocky headland on the northern coast of Tunis, north of Sidi Bou Said and La Marsa.
cap carthage.a: The rocky headland along the coast north of Sidi Bou Saïd and La Marsa, with its views of the sea and the coastline.
cap carthage.c: Beautiful sunset light; perfect for a stroll through Sidi Bou Saïd or La Marsa.

cap gammarth.d: The headland along the coast north of La Marsa, the cliffs and beaches of Gammarth.
cap gammarth.a: The cliffs and beaches of Gammarth, north of La Marsa, and the coastal views of the gulf.
cap gammarth.c: A pleasant place for a stroll along the seashore; a picturesque sunset on the coast.

parc ennahli.d: A large urban park and reforested area on the hills north of Tunis (Ariana), offering a panoramic view of the metropolitan area.
parc ennahli.a: The vast reforested area on the hills north of Tunis and its panoramic viewpoint overlooking the city and the lake.
parc ennahli.c: A popular spot for Sunday walks and picnics; unobstructed views on clear days.

djebel boukornine.d: A mountain with two peaks ("the two horns") overlooking Hammam Lif and the Gulf of Tunis.
djebel boukornine.a: The distinctive twin peaks (“the two horns”) overlooking Hammam Lif, its wooded trails, and the view of the Gulf of Tunis.
djebel boukornine.c: Hike through the heart of the national park; depart from Hammam Lif—bring water and sturdy shoes.

djebel marchana.d: The terrain in southern Ben Arous forms a nature reserve home to Mediterranean flora and fauna.
djebel marchana.a: The forested landscape of southern Ben Arous, designated as a nature reserve, and its Mediterranean flora and fauna.
djebel marchana.c: A natural area with few facilities for hikers; check for access information and bring water.

sebkha de rades.d: A salt marsh on the southern shore of Lake Tunis, near Rades, a peri-urban wetland.
sebkha de rades.a: The peri-urban salt marsh on the southern shore of Lake Tunis, frequented by waterfowl.
sebkha de rades.c: Wetland in an urban area: best viewed from the surrounding area; of particular interest to birdwatchers in winter.

sebkha kourzia.d: Large sebkha in the western part of the Zaghouan Governorate (El Fahs region), a seasonal wetland.
sebkha kourzia.a: The large seasonal sebkha in western Zaghouan (El Fahs region) and its salt flats and marshes, which vary depending on the season.
sebkha kourzia.c: Best viewed after it has rained, when the water level is high; birdwatching from the surrounding area.

cat.Islamique (XVIIe s. sur fondation mediev: Islamic (17th century, built on medieval foundations)
cat.Ottomane (XVIe s., sur fondations anteri: Ottoman (16th century, built on earlier foundations)
